reviews.review:
I've been to Tempura Matsui twice now and recommended it to friends who absolutely loved it. Even my boyfriend, who *hates* fish, was a fan of their fish tempura! I've been for both lunch and dinner--lunch has fewer courses but is still incredibly fulfilling, and you'll definitely have a food baby walking out of there. Definitely ask for counter seating if you go for dinner (sometimes they'll sit you at a booth if the counter fills up).

The service here is absolutely impeccable. They guide you through each course, explaining the best way to enjoy everything. One of my favorite touches: they helped me plate my food to take pictures, paying such great attention to detail. They even gave me a little spoon to scoop the salt over my tempura so I wouldn't mess up my manicure (without me mentioning it) and refilled me lemon juice since they saw me taking some of my boyfriend's. We also got a little nice dessert from them for our special day. It's those little details that make it stand out.

They also change some of their ingredients seasonally, so it's nice to try something new each time--though the shrimp tempura is always a constant, and it's *amazing*.

Excellent tempura. Likely the best in the city.

Very classy 2 hour lunch with a filling meal covering all tempuras. Well worth the experience and been here a few times

Food is great, but idk if it justifies the price. You start with a pretty interesting soup, then some sashimi, then all kind of tempura. You get seafood, vegetables, etc. All tempura is delicious. Also it's cool that they fry everything in the middle of the dining area but you can't smell the frying oil at all. Then you will get some don and dessert at the end. For the rice, you can choose between soy sauce and a tea one (like you pour tea in your rice); I personally like the soy sauce more. I don't really like their dessert because it has a strong alcohol taste. It's a very small place so might be hard to get reservation.

We have eaten here many times and each time the experience is fantastic. Chef Endo and his assistant are wonderful, hardworking hosts. Every dish is perfection. The decor is so beautiful. We love eating here knowing we will have a truly memorable evening.

I was a bit apprehensive about going here initially since I'm not the biggest tempura fan. Don't get me wrong, I love freshly fried shrimp tempura any day. But a whole tasting menu with all tempura dishes?. They have a Michelin star, so maybe they know what they are doing here. My girlfriend loves tempura and we were bummed that we had to skip on an amazing tempura experience in Kyoto, so I thought this would be a great alternative a few years later.

I got to say, this place may have converted me into a tempura believer. Every course was fried perfectly and the accompaniments were a great balance. I never thought all of those courses would fill me up, but I finished that meal barely able to move. The decor here makes you think you're back in Japan as well. Friendly chefs and waiters makes it all a great experience.

Lil not sure how best to describe the restaurant instead of the best tempura. They offer authentic tempura, not a fry, that comes with perfect service. Price is well justified for its quality and volume and it is a bargain to enjoy this quality without flying to Japan.
10 generations of MasterChef have made this place what it is. One of the best meals I've had in my life highly highly highly recommend eating here.

It's worth mentioning that our server, Mr. San, was very professional and explained all the dishes in detail. Overall, it was a very nice and professional experience.

We made a reservation for two for Saturday lunch. The restaurant's capacity is around 12 people, and the decor was nice.

We ordered the lunch menu, which included pumpkin sauce with scallops, sashimi, rice with soup, dessert, and a combination of tempura. It was my first time trying all the tempura at once, and it was really worth it. We also ordered uni from the menu, priced at $35 each, and it was definitely worth it.

One of our party members had just graduated with a PhD, so the restaurant provided us with a special cake.

The decor and the environment are a bit outdated. However, everything is clean and well maintained, no easy task given that they have to fry things regularly. 

The service is friendly and prompt. The food is obviously good (frying things usually makes everything good). The reasons I only give 4 stars is because of the price point and the fact that nothing really makes this place extraordinary. It's worth a go if you miss traditional Japanese tempura but doesn't warrant a return trip.

Had a very good experience at tempura matsui. Service is great, they're on top of everything while making you feel very comfortable. I sat at the counter, everyone is served simultaneously and it's fun watching chef cook every piece perfectly. At the end you're able to add extra pieces of things you enjoyed or others not served on the menu. Favorite bites were - maitake, squid, the two fish sets (one with sujiko), and the scallop.

Excellent ambiance and impeccable service allowing the chef to showcase the star of the show: the food. Tempura Matsui has the perfect tempura batter: light and crunchy, allowing the flavor of the food to shine through and not overpowering it. This is why I keep coming back.
this place is insane.  amazing food, service was impeccable, beverages were amazing.  this is one of the most fun and delicious lunches I've been to.

I wondered what could warrant a tempura restaurant garnishing a Michelin star. But any doubt, though I really had one, was quickly erased as we entered. Quintessential Japanese hospitality and attention to detail was evident within moments. The amazing welcome and service my 10 year old received were that of the highest standard while making him comfortable to be in such an upscale setting surrounded by nothing but older adults. The tempura, immaculate! From fried fish bones, to shrimp legs, king crab in shiso leaf, perfectly cooked scallops, eel, hen of the woods mushrooms(my sons favorite and the kid refuses to eat mushrooms at home), sweet potato, shrimp, all lightly battered and served with a accompaniments of salts and sauces with instructions from the staff on what to put on each dish. The Chawanmushi, always a favorite of mine, comes with choices...foie gras or seafood. Both were fantastic. The meal finished with a first for me, the very expensive crown melon. Lightly seeet and juicy. I cannot recommend this place enough because it does something that very few restaurants can do, take something that I think I am familiar with and elevate it to unimaginable heights. Isn't that what we all chase with each bite we take.

Spetacular lunch at Tempura Matsui! I have lived near the restaurant for years and never visited due to the notion that it will always be there, but boy am I glad I finally did! The restaurant holds a very well deserved star and I was thoroughly enjoying every bite.

The meal begins with some sashimi that was very high quality, then many courses of tempura, then a tempura rice bowl with a choice of sauce, and ends with a refreshing dessert. 

Highlights include the various seafood courses which went extremely well with the seasoning, and the strong hospitality by the staff who come by to instruct diners on how to enjoy each ingredient.

I was in New York for a Business Trip and wanted to have a last night with an intimate quiet and calm ambiance. I decided to find an Omakase. I'm not a fan of Tempura but thought it would be good to step out of my comfort zone. The restaurant entrance is cute and the restaurant itself is small and intimate as expected.

The service is exceptional with waiters acting as co-pilot to describe the food coming to you. The chefs are 2, quiet and very focused on the food.

When I think of Tempura, I think about this fat yellow fried paste around a shrimp in some cheap sushi japanese restaurants and it's not something I like. Deciding to come was a choice and any doubt was removed right at the start. This is not what you will get.

They started to make shrimp heads fried but literally just a way down and up in hot oil like a fondue and it was just crispy and delicious!

Then they bring you some delicious sashimis, a shawan mushi with uni and some caviar. The omakase is 23 courses with fish, mushroom and more. Everything is presented amazingly and you feel extra full at the end. Your plate is provided with few ingredients to help to season the food with different salts, lemon and more.

Overall I loved it, the price ($280+tax+tip+wine) is on the upper hand but overall worth the experience. The French wine was good but not too generous and it needs to be fixed. This is definitely a one/two Michelin star.

Five star service, food, and experience. The staff are so attentive and made us feel so welcome. They explained every dish with detail and gave us suggestions on the best way to eat it. 

The food was amazing. Everything was cooked so well and seasoned. It's really a different and new experience for omakase since it's usually sushi. The tempura was fried perfectly. 

One thing I just want to highlight is the care and attention the staff put in. I called in a few days ago to ask what could be done for a birthday celebration and when I arrived at the restaurant, the waiter remembered me. They gave us an extra mini dessert for the birthday person. 

It is a bit pricey so I definitely recommend the lunch session. The lunch portion was more than enough to fill the average person up. Also I'd recommend requesting the counter seating if you make a reservation. It's a cooler experience to sit infront of the chef. 

It was truly a great experience and I would happily come back again!

Tempura Matsui is an outstanding restaurant that definitely earned its Michelin star.  The food is excellent and service is absolutely top-notch.  It has a very intimate and comfortable atmosphere.  It is not large.  There are perhaps 8 seats at the Tempura bar, then three or four tables--so obviously get reservations early.  You can see the chefs from anywhere (who work non-stop).

The restaurant is kind of hidden with just a single door and not a big sign (there is photo with the review).  It is a set menu at a steep price ($280 per person), but you get what you pay for.  You get a lot of different tastes and will leave full.  Also pay attention to name of restaurant.  A big portion of food is tempura--which I love, but may not be for everybody.  

As you would expect, most of the drink menu features sake.  I am not a fan, so we had red wine.  They also had some good mocktails.

Bring an appetite.  There is a lot of courses and tastings.  We started with an Amuse-bouche.  This included two wonderful bites.  One was a form of tofu that had an original and wonderful flavor and the other was some squid that I think was boiled.  The key here was the other ingredients they added for wonderful bites and it also looked beautiful.

Next was sashimi.  This was so good, I would not have minded more.  This included some of the best tuna I have had (it just melted in your mouth) and then snapper that was also great.  Presentation was again gorgeous and they had a flower that we sprinkled over the sashimi.

Next was a steam egged custard, where we choose seafood (with caviar on top).  This was very rich and the flavor was good, but not one of my personal favorites.

After that, the tempura started.  This included almost every kind of seafood prepared just perfect, with just the lightest of coatings.  It was really perfect.  For the setup, they had a seaweed kind of salt, some tempura sauce (with radishes poured in), and then fresh lemon juice (where they had this cute juicer for you to squeeze fresh).  

It started with Shrimp heads and then shrimp.  Both excellent.  Then I do not remember the exact order, but other tempura included snow crab, white asparagus, cod (or another white fish), scallops, potato, and some kind of green vegetable.  I may be missing something, but it was a lot and so tasty.  Definitely the best tempura I have ever had. 

After that, was a rice dish that you could have one of three ways, with truffle salt, with tea, or another way.  I had the tea because it sounded so odd.  It turned out to be really good.  I poured the tea in an it covered the rice, then provided a really good complement to the shrimp.  I am not sure what tea they used and if this could be replicated, but it was an amazing flavor.

After that, was dessert.  Ours was just melon.  I was maybe expecting more, but I was kind of full and it was a really good melon (kind of a honeydew, but I guess imported from Japan).

This place may not be for everyone.  One of the people in the party who is not a huge fan of seafood thought it was overwhelming--and perhaps a couple more vegetables mixed into tempura could help.  Then some of the food was exotic, like the shrimp heads and the custard, but part of why you go to these type of extraordinary restaurants should be to try foods you will not get anywhere else.

So if you want the best tempura you ever had in a wonderful setting with great service, Tempura Matsui cannot be beat.

Came here for a surprise birthday lunch.

Menu:
Shrimp head
Shrimp
Mushroom
Fish with the bones (?)
Snow Crab with Shiso Leaf
Brussel Sprout with Seaweed(?)
Scallop
Snow pea & Baby Onion
Flying fish
Lotus
Anago
Tendon with miso

Wasn't incredibly oily at the end of everything, I had a beer to go with my meal as a palette cleanser.
Service was great, showed great attention to customers. Chefs were attentive, and notice when you want a good video shot at the whole frying process and try not to ruin your video.  As a small extra birthday surprise, added a nice large strawberry with a mochi ice cream. 
Great experience, would love to try again someday.

When my boyfriend told me we were going to eat here, I was a bit skeptical. I felt like for that price maybe we should just have went to eat at an omakase place instead of one where everything was fried, but boy was I wrong. We were seated immediately upon entry. I wish I wasn't currently on crutches as I would've loved to sit at the bar and watch the chefs make the oh so delicate tempura.

There were five or six courses, but each course felt like there was 500 things in there, so here are my favorite food parts of the meal. 
- Tempura favorites:

- Shokuji Tencha - When they gave all the options for what to eat the last rice dish with, I was a bit worried of ordering the tencha as I thought it might dilute all the flavors and make it very watery. I was completely wrong and it was unequivocally the best option there. The tea itself, although very light, when paired with the green tea salt and the flavorful tempura completely elevated the dish as it became almost like a broth. It was a perfect ending to the meal as it showed the skills of the tempura master as well as the beautiful flavors of the green tea.
- Melon - When they brought out the melon at the end, my boyfriend and I both looked at each other like uhh... this is our dessert? We were so wrong to estimate the melon. If they brought out ice cream or some cake, I think we would've been too full to eat it, but melon? It was the most perfect dessert item as the melon was incredibly succulent, it literally melts in your mouth. On first bite, all the juices flow out of the melon and it feels like you're drinking the most fresh melon juice of your life. I'm still dreaming about this one.

But what is a Michelin-starred restaurant without all the ambiance surrounding the food? Here are my favorite parts of the experience other than the food:
- The toilet seats were warm! I know this is so weird, but I loved the toilets as they felt so clean, neat, and fancy. 
- Our server was incredibly knowledgeable of everything on the menu and I absolutely loved that he taught us how to best eat each of the tempura pieces as I really think his pairing and knowledge elevated each piece. Also, he was extremely attentive. The minute we finished our tempura piece, he would arrive with another one. It was a never-ending tempura journey, and I was here for it.
- Okay this is kind of cheating, but I absolutely love all the dipping sauce options. I loved that there were 2 kinds of salt and you can really tell the difference between them.
- I loved the lemon juicer haha. I thought it was such a fancy way not to get your fingers dirty but still maximize all the juices in the lemon. Also, it was such a satisfying thing to squeeze it all out.

If I come back next time, I will just come for lunch as it is $100 cheaper and the food seems to be roughly the same minus the Chawanmushi which is not that big of a deal.

10/10 experience! We booked it for a dinner and got seating at the bar where the frying station is, they also have booth seating but I def preferred the bar seating. They go over which salts is best accompanied with which piece and all the pieces came out at a good pace. The service is amazing here and they are very attentive! The chefs were nice and I had so many favorite pieces! The tempura omakase was such a unique experience! I was stuffed at the end of the meal and the frying doesn't feel greasy at all! It is pricy but it's a good celebratory meal!

Splurge on the most refined tempura with quality ingredients in a light airy batter and accompanying dishes of varying textures and flavors that balance out the meal. It's a good thing when the only complaint is possibly overeating. The decor is traditional and not fancy or stuffy at this intimate establishment. The service is thoughtful if not entirely seamless. Overall a welcoming relaxed and delicious experience.

I used to be THE best tenpura in town also probably in the states like high quality tenpura restaurants in Japan.  But I was very disappointed this time and wouldn't go back again.  Unlike when Mr. Matsui had been in charge, the overall quality of ingredients and the skill of the chef were second rates at best.  The tare on the tendon didn't have any umami. It was just like sugared water.  Maybe it was!  The bottom like is the price has gone up but the quality has gone way down.  I would suggest to eat cheaply 10 times at Ootoya (30 times in Japan!) instead with the same amount of money you must pay just for a meal there.

The only Michelin star omakase tempura!!

It's not cheap at $250 a person before tax and tip but each piece is fried to perfection. It comes at a good pace and its unique setting for omakase. 

Felt a little hefty after though with all the oil but def worth checking out at least once.

Incredible. I had high expectations because it's a Michelin reviewed restaurant, but not so much since I don't have tempura that often. What a beautiful dining experience - from the presentation of the most gorgeous sake sakazuki glass I have ever seen, the service of having every dish explained, and the the delicateness of the thin layers of tempura that make me question every other piece of tempura I've had prior.

To get straight to the point, Tempura Matsui serves a $300 tempura dinner, omakase style. The price is steep, but the incredible tempura and the personalized service is well worth the price of admission. Each course is a delightful play on traditional tempura, with no parts of the seafood off limits. Seating is extremely limited so reserve in advance, and definitely call ahead to reserve the lobster supplement to the prix fixe or you'll regret it.

Came here for dinner omakase with my wife. Easily the best tempura we've ever had. The service and ambiance were worthy of a Michelin Star. But be warned, you will be very full by the end of the meal. Do not add the lobster to your meal, UNLESS you have a massive appetite. My wife and I struggled once the last quarter of the meal arrived, but I somehow caught a second wind with the final 2 courses because the food was so delicious. If we skipped the lobster, I think we would've been fine.

TLDR: Bottom-line, it is so much more than a tasting of fried tempura. If you've never had proper tempura before, you are missing out. You may find this to be equally as enjoyable as a true omakase.

I figured for the 500th review, it should be a happy one. I had Tempura Matsui bookmarked for more than 10 years. To call it just a tempura menu does not do it justice. If you have never been to a true tempura restaurant (hard to find outside of Japan), the precision cooking and preparation that goes into it is another level. To be candid, I actually enjoyed this more than both tempura tastings I've had in Tokyo. We came for lunch and so glad we did. Easily top 5 meals of 2023.

At $160 pp it is a lot of food and really a great value for the kind of ingredients and expertise you're getting. Starters were a Japanese potato salad with salmon roe and a sashimi plate. Both excellent.

The tempura progression starts right away and the service was fantastic. Each piece as it came out was explained, advised on how to enjoy it for optimum flavor and all the different salts, condiments, etc. Each piece and the recommended salt/sauce pairing is very intentional. Each tempura is cooked to the precise timing to maximize the quality of the ingredient, provide a crispy exterior while maintaining an overall light palette feel to the meal.

There was not a bad piece but typically the fried shrimp heads start first. So delicate, the crispy legs with the hot inside is a great starter. The maitake mushroom with the natural sprigs provides for maximum crunch and a deep earthy umami flavor. The Japanese whiting is light/fleshy with the bone fried out where it's basically a fish chip for extra crispiness. The sweet king crab leg wrapped in shiso is sweet, refreshing, crispy all at once. The Japanese eggplant was so elegantly crisp on the outside but piping hot on the inside. I especially enjoyed the recommendation to tear it open and stuff it with the bonito flakes for a flavor bomb sandwich if you will. The sea eel though, nice and big with so many crispy clusters and almost creamy-like texture on the meat. Sea eel is my favorite tempura piece, period.

You can opt to get the fried tempura cluster over rice or tendon or the tempura and tea over rice. I recommend the tendon. Tendon is half the reason to even go to a tempura tasting. We all know the best part of an omakase (outside of the tuna) is the hand roll. If there's no hand roll, it feels like a miss. Like who wants a burger without the fries?

The grapefruit jelly pudding was the perfect way to cleanse the palette and end on a note overly sweet note. Tempura Matsui is a place I'd recommend if you're into Japanese food, fine dining or just great food period. My only regret, I should have started coming here way earlier.

We came for a Friday lunch and was seated at the bar. Able to watch the chef work his tempura magic. Tempura was lightly battered to perfection and the perfect internal temperature. Definitely the most extensive tempura selection I've ever eaten.

I enjoyed that they had two options for how to eat the tempura, the dashi with tempura dip or lemon and salt. Seafood paired well with the lemon since it's less overpowering. The tempura dip was also absolutely magical. 
Beancurd with roe
Tuna, toro, octopus - from Toyosu market. 
Shrimp head - excellent

eggplant

One of the most unique meals I've ever had. Tempura Matsui presents a pretty incredible Michelin-starred meal that impresses from start to finish. The experience is omakase-style and features seasonal ingredients in a multi-course tasting. Given the name of the restaurant, expect a ton of lightly battered deep fried pieces. The service was attentive and the restaurant itself is fairly intimate and quiet. A lot of emphasis is placed on the presentation of the food and your server will give suggested pairings/seasonings. It's a pricey meal but definitely think it's worth going at least once if you're into tempura. However, if you're not into tempura or deep fried things I'm not sure if this restaurant will change your mind.

I was in New York again last week, and three of us went here for dinner. Knowing that this place has maintained a Michelin Star status since 2016, we were excited to indulge in some fantastic tempura. The meal comprised 18 courses, starting with a Hokkaido uni, quail egg, and mountain yam amuse-bouche, followed by a substantial slab of herring roe on a bed of mustard greens topped with bonito flakes. It was a fantastic start to an excellent meal.
Next up was a plate of sashimi with four pieces, featuring Japanese amberjack, bluefin tuna, and chu toro--each piece was fresh, buttery, and silky, simply fantastic! Following that, we were served chawan mushi, a steamed egg custard, with the option to choose between foie gras or seafood. Two of us opted for foie gras, while one chose seafood. The foie gras-infused chawan mushi had small chunks of foie, and the seafood variant was brimming with delicious shellfish. Both were exquisite.
The real highlight, however, was the tempura courses. It started with ama-ebi (two heads), perfectly crispy and utterly delicious. Then, we were served the shrimp bodies one at a time, showcasing the delicate and sweet kuruma shrimp. The parade continued with Maitake mushrooms, Kisu fish with perfectly fried bones, snow crab wrapped in shiso, corn tempura, scallops, Matsutake mushrooms, eel, and many more. By the time I reached the scallops, I was absolutely stuffed!
We were also treated to Japanese eggplant with ginger bonito and, of course, oyster tempura, along with more tempura dishes. To our surprise, after all this tempura indulgence, we were asked to choose a main dish. It seemed almost comical after the feast we just had. I mean, who in their right mind, or stomach in this case, decided that they were still hungry after all these tempura courses and wanted yet another dish with more tempura, but this time, over a bowl of rice?? LOL Despite being completely stuffed, we took a bite of the main dish. I must admit that the rice was perfectly cooked, a testament to a great Asian restaurant. The dessert was a simple slice of Japanese crown melon. I've had these $100 melons in Japan and these were the same kind, but the sweet intensity that you get from the ones in Japan are incomparable. However these were very good compared to the best of the American honeydew melons variety. It was a sweet and refreshing way to end the meal.
The entire meal was outstanding, and the service was efficient and attentive. However, I felt that the tempura courses were served too quickly. I would have preferred a more leisurely pace, but the head chef and sous chef were diligently preparing and serving dishes as soon as diners finished. I even intentionally slowed down my eating, but I still received the next dish before I had finished my current one.
Overall, the restaurant was excellent, and the food was delicious. If you expect to leave a Japanese restaurant hungry due to small portions, this place will surprise you. You'll leave fully satisfied, perhaps even waddling out the door. Personally, I would prefer if they reduced the number of tempura courses and charged less. However, I understand that with fewer than 20 seats in the restaurant, they need to charge a certain amount to cover their costs. The omakase price per person is $280, and our bill, including drinks, came to $985 plus tip. It's not a budget-friendly place, but you'll leave with a full stomach and a satisfied palate. I think I'm "tempura'd" out for the next entire year! LOL

I was torn about giving this place a three star review. It's got the fine dining service, but it's not quite there with the food, which unfortunately doesn't meet with the price.  

The idea of a Michelin Starred tempura restaurant was really intriguing to me. I love Japanese food and tempura. So, being able to attend a Michelin starred dining experience was right in the wheelhouse of my 4 person family.  

The amuse and sashimi were outstanding.  The grade of fish they used for the sashimi was unparalleled.  The fish was cut perfectly. Its taste and texture was a once in a lifetime experience.   

The tempura started well enough with the shrimp heads and the full pieces of shrimp, which was everyone's favorite.  The rest of the tempura included some of the usual suspects, but also a couple of lesser known surprises, such as shaved corn.   

The issue I had was that each successive dish was adding to the total amount of grease consumed so it became increasingly less appetizing.  The maitake mushroom probably held onto the most fry grease, so it was particularly heavy.  

You're given somewhere between 12-15 different fried items, which is a lot of food.  (Some of the dishes come with two items on the plate).  Part of me thinks they give you so much food to try to legitimize the price of the omakase.  I think it just makes you feel less satisfied at the end of the meal.  

The dessert they provided at the end of the meal was a slice of Japanese melon, which I think was cut too close to the rind, which made it harder to chew and reduced the overall sweetness of the melon.  

As I said at the start, the service was top tier.  The ambience and decor were perfect. But the taste of the food and the price would prevent me from going back there a second time.

I had a truly fun and warm experience at this small restaurant and thoroughly enjoyed the food as well but at this price point the menu left me wanting a bit more.

Tempura Matsui features a central counter seating 10 as well as just a few tables. It is on the casual side for an upscale omakase but not in a negative way. There is gentle jazz music in the background which combines with the ever-present crackle of the tempura oil and hearkens to a cozy winter day indoors. 

I was lucky to get a same day reservation and called ahead to express my preference for the counter.  When I got there the host joked that I was the man who demanded the counter, probably recognizing my voice. All night this guy was super attentive and really drove home the experience. The rest of the staff are on point but there is room for a bit more finesse at this level of dining. My countertop was always clean and my drink was always full but it could have all just been a bit sharper.

The menu weighs in at a hefty 250pp before tax and tip. This includes some sashimi selections, chawanmushi, tempura omakase with a parade of sauces/seasonings, and a rice dish in that order.

The highlights included...
Foie Gras Chawanmushi - Just incredible. Hot, rich, silky and balanced.
Maitake mushroom - possibly my favorite individual piece of the night. It has a meaty, umami flavor and just disappears on the tongue.
My wife does not eat abalone - the substitute they brought was a generous serving of uni! very classy
The Hokkaido Scallop - did not gain much from the tempura batter but was one of the sweetest and tastiest I have ever had.

Some things that could have been better...
I wish the shrimp head had more meat inside to bring that juiciness. The uni wrapped in bass was good but I would much prefer a tempura dish topped with cold, delicious uni. For the price point and simplicity of cooking, I would have wanted a few more exotic ingredients. Finally, I was excited to see how a dedicated tempura spot at this level would deliver its take on dessert - unfortunately we were presented with an out-of-season honeydew and the opportunity was wasted.

Overall worth a visit for a unique experience and truly delicious food but Tempura Matsui did not wow me as much as I hoped.

Tempura Matsui is an intimate experience located in New York City. The moment you arrive at the location, you can already tell that it's very different from other places with its unique exterior and cozy interior. 
The staff greets you warmly and welcomes you and sits you at your chosen seat. As I went with my girlfriend for New Years, I had chosen booth seats for us. The restaurant is small and quaint and fits about 20 people not including the staff. You also have the option to sit at the tempura counter and watch the master tempura chefs as they work. 
Now, as this is an Omakase experience, follow the instructions of your hosts. Take their suggestions as they are absolutely on point. Every suggestion was made with care and in order to help you enjoy the food to the absolute max.
The food was amazing. Everything that was served to us, there was nothing left. From our initial dish which was a salmon roe soup, to our final dessert, a delicious Japanese honey melon, there was not one complaint about the food.
Because of the unique nature of the restaurant, we even got to try things we never had tried before such as fish head, fish bones, urchin. Everything about this place was something I still unconsciously compare other restaurants to.
To me, the service was second to none. This was the most exceptional service I have ever experienced. Never in my life have I ever been treated the way I was here. And to that, I thank the staff.
If you are ever in NYC and are looking for an authentic Tempura Omakase experience, this is the place.

I was visiting NYC for a week and Tempura Matsui was my favorite meal of the trip! The $160 lunch was a steal with plenty of food.

To start off there was a tofu skin dish and a few pieces of sashimi. I don't think I've had such yummy tofu skin before and the toro melted in my melt. 

It was memorizing to sit at the bar and watch the chefs work. Each dish was exquisite and it's so hard to pick a favorite. Something we had never had before was uni tempura and it was just as amazing as it sounds. I was dining with someone who isn't the biggest fan of shrimp, but he said this was the best shrimp he's ever had.

Highly highly recommend Tempura Matsui! It is hands down the best tempura I've had in the US and comparable to the tempura from Japan. The service and food was impeccable! Very deserving of its Michelin Star.

A lovely small restaurant with wonderful customer service and delicious food. The interior is intimate and warm, with wood and ceramics. The workers tell you the best way to eat each dish. They were friendly and helpful.

The lunch omakase included tempura of a variety of seafood (fish, eel, sea urchin, shrimp in lotus root) corn (summer), mushroom (very light and crunchy), cucumber (hot), etc. It was all delicious.

Dessert was a grapefruit jelly with cream.

There is tasty cold smokey tea drink that isn't too sweet.

There are two bathrooms. They take card.

Food is excellent. Setting is a bit austere, even for a Japanese restaurant but dinner prices are excessive. Staff is professional from beginning to end.
Plenty of excellent tempura in other NYC spots.

Tempura omakase restaurant with an authentic atmosphere.   Attentive Japanese staff and the service was excellent.   We chose counter seats and two chefs cooking right in front of us.   Everything was meticulously prepared and executed to perfection.   I didn't expect so much food.   Was so full after the meal!!    Go hungry.   See my pics for the dinner courses.

Tempura !!! Walking into Matsui was like walking into a restaurant in Kyoto, Japan. The greeting was warm ( even though we were a few minutes late) and the staff attentive, knowledgeable and fun. Saki recommendation was excellent, and direction on how to proceed and eat the sumptuous meal we're thorough. 
Not sure why I waited a Month to write this review but I will let the pictures do the talking...
I would say if you are lucky enough to get a reservation just enjoy the experience, trust the staff and let your taste buds indulge.

Overall a good but not amazing dinner/experience at Tempura Matsui considering the price point and reputation. We ordered the omakase course which consists of appetizer, sashimi, chef's selection of tempura, shokuji, and then dessert. I will mainly highlight the tempura, which consisted of the following the night we went: 

Shrimp head
Shrimp body w salt and lemon juice
Shrimp body with tempura sauce and radish
Maitake mushroom
Kisu tempura with bone
Shiso leaf with snow crab dipped in lemon juice
Cabbage tempura dipped in sauce
Japanese red snapper with shallot pickles
Hokkaido scallop with truffle salt
Chopped shrimp
Eggplant
Barracuda
Tile fish
Chrysanthemum greens

Some favorites among the meal was the kisu (whitefish), red snapper, and cabbage. While I didn't feel any of the pieces were actively bad, I felt all of them were pretty one note in flavor. I was disappointed by some pieces like the scallop, which I felt was overcooked. My biggest complaint is every piece was too hot. I literally burned my mouth eating each piece, which wasn't something I experienced at some other tempura spots. We also were sitting at a booth, so there was some time for it to cool before arriving to the table. It was definitely hard to enjoy the meal when I was just burning my mouth the entire time.

The service is super attentive. Servers clear your plate with a new one after a few pieces. They also direct you on how to eat each piece, whether to dip in salt, sauce, or lemon juice, etc. The experience was a bit overkill for my friend whom I dined with. I'm not sure if the counter experience is any better.

For $300, we left full but disappointed by the food and experience. There was definitely a higher expectation that wasn't met. I hate to compare, but I prefer Secchu Yokota for tempura omakase.

I love GOOD tempura, and the tempura here is made perfectly. I was able to dine right in front of the tempura chefs and they take such care in getting the pieces perfectly fried and not too soggy/crisp. Light and airy. I dined here in November 2022 and really enjoyed it. Would definitely come back if I want perfect tempura! So hard to get this kind of quality. Rest of menu was also good - like the uni/foie gras.

Tempura Matsui is as close as you can get to a true tempura experience that you would have with a tempura master in Japan. We have been going to Tempura Kondo in Tokyo for many years. Tempura Matsui almost achieves the same level of quality that we have come to expect from a tempura master like Kondo-sensei. Tempura Matsui is not inexpensive, but it is worth every penny and certainly less than a flight to Tokyo.

I want to love Tempura Matsui because the staff/service was phenomenal, the place had an intimate vibe with great lighting and low noise levels, and it's a freaking 1 star Michelin tempura place (how common are these?). The tempura technique and food were great, but not worth the $90 lunch price and certainly not worth the new increased lunch price of $160 (unless they've made significant modifications).

You better be vegetarian leaning as 70% of these dishes are single fried pieces of veggies. At that price range, I was expecting a lot more protein so I felt quite ripped off. The food was good, don't get me wrong, but feels like they slapped on a premium for their airy tempura frying technique that's commonplace in Japan for a fraction of the price. 

TLDR; great tempura, but not at this price range, unless you have money to spend and/or pregame heavily beforehand so you can pretend you had a full meal at this price.

Everything about this experience was great. I called ahead to see if there were any reservations but they are booked for weeks. The guy on the phone was very polite and accommodating and said if anything opened he would call me. An hour later he called to let me know a reservation opened. My family and I were traveling from California and the host asked which days and times we would be in New York which showed me he actually cared to help me. We walked into a beautiful restaurant. Each person greeted us. Our server was very attentive. He explained the menu and each dish that came out he told us how it is usually eaten (what to dip the tempura in). The menu is omakase  and looked small and was a little over $200 per person. By time the entree came we were so full. This was the best food we ate the entire trip. I will definitely be back and would recommend this to anyone. 
Thank for a dinner to remember

Highly highly recommend this 1 star michelin tempura place!! I have eaten at many tempura spots in Japan & this is AUTHENTIC! Not just authentic, but exceptional! They deserve their michelin but more.

I took my sister here for the lunch special to celebrate her early birthday. Per staff, today 11/26 was the last day for the $80 lunch special.  Staff told us it will be $160 for lunch special starting 11/27, so we were lucky. Honestly, with the quality and the amount of food it is worth the price! The service and attentiveness was exceptional! 

We were luck to sit in the front area & got to watch all the action. We ordered a draft sapporo & apple hichu cocktail and both were delicious! The 1st meal came out and it was a a beautiful tray full of many delicious items: salmon, scallop, udon noodle, steamed egg custard (chawanmushi), shio salt and tempura dipping sauce. They had 10 random tempura pieces (shrimp, mushroom, lotus root, eggplant, snapper, some japanese white fish with deep fried bone (shocked the fish bone was delish), a fish that looks like eel wrapped with seaweed, a shrimp shiso ball thing, cabbage). Afterward, they give u a nice hot hojicha tea then a dessert (we had something like a grapefruit gelee panna cotta). P.S - that last cabbage tempura item which is their signature tempura shocked us to the core - it was so unique and delicious!

Every single item was exceptional and so damn delicious! Even my sister who does not like to eat fish, liked the fish tempuras. 

Staff was exceptional and very attentive and friendly. I always love the japanese hospitality and always feel the love whenever I eat at a Japanese restaurant in NYC or Japan.
Amazing! Best tempura I've had in my life. Highly recommend it. Great service. Great meal.

Great service and great food.  You leave very full, do not need to order the lobster lol. The tempura is extremely light and fluffy--just like my experience in Japan! 

It is very hard to find this type of tempura around. Tempura at restaurants are usually caked with batter and makes me feel bloated after eating it. There was a large variety of different tempura dishes.  Be careful when eating--can be extremely hot!

I didn't take pictures of all tempra course but you can tell how this place made me excited. 

It was Friday lunch. I called them 30mins before and the chef allowed me to squeeze in. 

I'm Japanese and I think this place made me feel back home. This situation (sit at the bar and served piece by piece) is special in Japan too. So the price can be as expensive as this place so you aren't missing anything. 

Appetizers were wonderful, I didn't eat udon tho-that was a bit weird to see on the tray but I think it was for ppl with bigger appetite. I highly recommend to enjoy their rice instead of udon. You might think just "rice" but even that rice is cooked perfectly. 

I just wish I had some pickles and miso soup to end the meal with the rice but that can be just because I'm too Japanese. 

I'm hoping one day they open their restaurant in Bay Area, CA.

At long last we found a tempura omakase restaurant. We had just discovered this type of restaurant / cuisine our last couple years in Hong Kong and fell in love. There are none in the Bay Area and there is one in LA but I've heard it's not the same. This one had a Michelin star and was the best yet. Every bite was absolutely amazing. Two types of prawn, two types of fish, and a million things inbetween. The batter was absolutely perfect on every piece. Crispy, but light and airy. Not even close to oily. The highlights were a chopped shrimp patty sandwiched by two pieces of lotus root. Completely unexpected and a textural masterpiece. So much crunch. The scallop was maybe one of the best bites I've food I've ever had. Perfectly cooked. Tender. The fried uni wrapped in seaweed was amazing. Uni is maybe the purest form and representation of the sea and it's taste of anything. The abalone was definitely the best piece of abalone I've ever had. It was soft but still had a little bounce / chew to it. What an amazing meal here at Tempura Matsui. If you like tempura, you must come here. You won't regret it.

Taste: *****
Service: ****
Ambiance: ****

Tempura Matsui
222 E 39th St, New York, NY 10016
----------------------------

This is the place that serve real tempura. (NOT those fake tempura with thick flour skin and American ingredients.

Traditional tempura sauce with sphere radish ball comes with different kinds of authentic Japanese food ingredients. i.e. shrimp head, white fish, crispy fish spine, abalone and even sea urchin. These are all used to make tempuras. In addition, the tempura skin is very thin and crispy. 

The service we experienced was extremely professional and decent.

Tempura is delicious here. The batter is light and they have a wide variety ranging from uni wrapped in seaweed to lotus roots to shrimp. I would definitely recommend trying the tempura omakase versus ordering a la carte. I ended up getting 2 a la carte items and although they were good, I would have been ok without it. The omakase also includes a rice dish topped with tempura and dessert. Our course even came with sashimi as our first dish.

Try to get there early and get counter seating. It's a cool experience seeing how they cook the tempura. Service was phenomenal. The server explained each item as it came out, how to eat the tempura (either with lemon and salt or tempura sauce), and made sure my cup of tea was never empty.

The lunch special is a steal. You can get top notch service and ingredients for under 100, including tax and tip. I left completely full and satisfied. Lunch booking is difficult and only two days a week but worth it. For how good the service was this place is closer to 2 stars

A reasonably priced lunch service ($65) at a Michelin-starred tempura restaurant? I was so happy I got a reservation. I love tempura so I personally found this worth it. Service was quite wonderful, so I won't mention it much. It was such a delight that I'll be doing my best to plan a visit here again.

Watching the tempura fry was so satisfying-- the oil was so clean and the batter looked so light. Just a two-man team frying for the whole counter of people. The overall meal pacing was nice and the tempura selections felt balanced. I appreciated hearing the staff's recommendations and descriptions throughout the meal.

The cocktail I added at the beginning pleasantly suited the mellow atmosphere. The cocktail was something sakura/cherry blossom themed, which I'm a sucker for. It tasted so smooth that I could hardly tell there was alcohol (and it might have been pretty low in alcohol for all I know). After the lunch set and tempura courses, I did add on some a la carte tempura at the end. Even though I was a little too full, I wanted to enjoy my stay longer.

A set lunch accompanied the tempura. The set lunch/bento had some udon, dipping sauces, and little amuse bouche-sized appetizers (?).

My favorite little details:
The dessert cups! I was delighted because they felt like rough granite, but they were more textured than rough. They were the perfect size for the panna cotta. If anyone knows where to find them, please let me know. I've never been in love with dishware before.

The soy jelly: It's one of those things that doesn't sound good as part of everyday cooking even though I think it would be great. This sat atop the fish in the lunch set. It tasted like ponzu-- at first I thought it was too salty, but then I was hit with tartness and sweetness. I want to make a batch of this at home for every piece of fish I eat from now on. It's funny because aspic (have you seen those terrifying recipes of meats in jellos?) has never sounded appealing to me but this was.

Simple notes on the lunch set:
Chawanmushi: had clams and edamame in it; interestingly enough had a hint of yuzu, can't go wrong with chawanmushi

Tuna: so good with the soy jelly, no fishy taste

Udon: perfect texture-- so bouncy and chewy

Simple notes on the tempura:
1. Shrimp tempura: good, surprised it could be a liiiittle salty

2. Maitake mushroom: good, tasted burnt but wasn't, not too mushroom-y, subtle

3. Cauliflower: good, so soft

4. Squid: good, chewy but not with an overcooked rubbery texture, hard to bite through cleanly so it wasn't crunchy either

5. Okra: good, my friend liked that it wasn't slimy

After the okra, they switched out the blotting paper on the presentation plate.

6. King salmon and shiso leaf: best with the accompanying salt, so nice with the soft juicy salmon against the tempura crunch

7. Japanese eggplant: good, really hot (a trend with moisture in vegetables heating it up so much?)

8. Anago/eel: really good, texture of overcooked white fish or something? but not quite as rubbery or chewy/weird-- just firm?; reminded me of my favorite restaurant for fried fish as a kid

9. Onion: good, simple/sweet

10. Shrimp/shiso fritter (aka kakiage): just the right amount of savoriness, juicy

Set menu ended and then I had my add-ons ($8 for two pieces each):

Shiitake: a little bitter but so good with tempura sauce, juicy
Lotus root: crunchy, solid, okay to try

Dessert was a mango panna cotta, with a mild sweetness and light mango flavor.

Tempura is very good. But when you feel there is something wrong with your dish (sand in your uni, or too salty in your shrimp) waiters won't try to fix it, they will just assume you are not used to what they are serving.

One of the most unique (and tastiest) Michelin experiences I've ever had!! Very small, intimate restaurant with just 3 booths and a few counter seats. We sat right at the counter and were able to watch the chefs cook the entire meal (highly recommend). 

The appetizers started with scallops, raw octopus, and a raw white fish. All tasted amazing but the raw octopus was unlike anything I've ever had; it was fresh and had a nice clean texture. After the appetizer course was your choice of a savory steamed egg custard- with either foie gras or seafood as the main ingredients. I tried both and thought they each had individual flavor profiles that were both delectable. The main course included about 10 items that were deep fried- including salmon, snow crab, asparagus, red snapper, lotus root, shrimp (2 types), mushrooms (2 types), snail (abalone), and Japanese whiting. I loved that they gave you a complete setup with 2 different ways (soy sauce variation or sea salt with lemon juice) to try each item (along with 2 pieces of that fish or veggies). 

The batter was unlike anything I've ever tasted. It was very light and airy, despite being "fried", and did not give me a stomach ache or fill me up too fast. It was interesting to me to watch the chefs first apply the batter to each item, coat it in liquid, and then add it to the oil (usually done in reverse order). After the main course we had one final rice dish- you were able to choose between 3 different preparations (tendon, tencha, or tenbara). I tried the option with the truffle salt and it did NOT disappoint (seaweed, rice, shrimp, truffle salt). For dessert we were served a grapefruit dish- I don't like grapefruit so I didn't eat mine and cannot comment on it.

Very wide selection of sake- if you like sake. Other than that, there was one seasonal cocktail, and a few wines to choose from. The atmosphere of this place was amazing, the service was impeccable, and the food was beyond perfection. Would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone that is a fan of Japanese food and/or seafood.

The best tempura you will ever eat outside of Japan. All around outstanding experience. We have gone twice for lunch and it was flawless both times. The tempura salmon is on my personal all time best bites list.

Being Japanese, I'm such a huge fan of authentic tempura and I'm glad there is a spot in NYC that serves light, crispy perfect tempura and not the heavy, greasy, oily tempura Americanized restaurants serve.  I reserved a spot for lunch well ahead of time (maybe a month or two ahead of time) and was the first one in the door for a reservation at noon.  Service is top-notch here as would be in Japan, and for $65 the lunch set is a good deal (versus $200 for dinner).  With tip and an extra additional order of $8, the bill came out to be just under $100. Would definitely come back to dine here!

This place was great! 

While initially I was frustrated that it was so hard to get a reservation, I appreciated the small dining space and the limited seating - it made the whole experience much more intimate. 

As expected of a Michelin restaurant, the service was excellent and the host and staff were well versed on each of the dishes. Our favorite were the abalone, shrimp head, and final don dish (I got mine with truffle salt which I can't recommend enough). 

If I had one complaint it would be that (as expected but may not register immediately) the food can be EXTREMELY hot. Some dishes with high water content (Uni and Zucchini) were unbearably hot and the staff don't give you a heads up. Eat with caution.

Would highly recommend this place especially if you are a fan of tempura. Very interesting take on the cuisine and loved the omakase format.
Excellent tempura for the US, though the ones I had in Tokyo are still superior. Still, I'd recommend it if you are a tempura aficionado.

Many tend to compare tempura matsui and Secchu Yokota. IMO both are high quality tempura in the city but my personal favorite is matsui. Tempura usually strike ppl as a greasy dish and the thought of finishing an entire omakase of tempura dishes can scare ppl away. However at Matsui, every dish is cooked simply to perfection. With the use of thin batter and precisely cooked seasonal ingredients, the chef made sure that the entire meal is well balanced and satisfying.

There are not enough good things to say about this place. I came here for lunch, and it was one of my best lunches of my life. The lunch set comes with a selection of appetizers, a selection of tempura, and dessert, all for $65. They first serve you the appetizer and explain to you how to eat each thing. Then throughout the meal each piece of tempura is placed on the plate in front of you omakase style. After each tempura is presented, the staff explains the best way to eat it. I just loved every part of this experience down to the decor. It felt like you were in a different world for your meal. It's definitely more than your average lunch but the service and quality of the food is worth it.

The quality of food, experience, and environment were truly excellent. Surprisingly however, I found that the highlights of my meal were not the tempura, but rather the sashimi starter and chawanmushi. The Amberjack sashimi was silky smooth, and the foie gras chawanmushi had so much umami, definitely one of the best japanese dishes I've ever had. 

The tempura itself was excellent, but a little monotonous. The maitake mushroom, pumpkin, and white fish were standouts, but it is hard for one to appreciate the nuances of each ingredient when every ingredient is prepared in the same style. Additionally, I felt as if the shrimp was a tad bland. Of course this is personal preference, but I would have preferred for a meal that was cheaper but had less tempura pieces. By the 5th or 6th piece, I felt like I had enough. 

Overall, an excellent dining experience and I would definitely recommend one to try this place. This is a place that I do not wish to return to because it is the uniqueness of the experience that makes Matsui worth it, but I'm so glad I had this experience.

Tempura Matsui is a cozy beautiful hideaway serving up omakase tempura lunch and dinner. Booked an early dinner slot for counter service.

Loved the Japanese teahouse decor with intricate wood ceiling and stone counters. The handmade pottery used for service made the experience aesthetically pleasing as well. Atmosphere was friendly yet casual, and our server Fumiyo gave us a few pointers on when and how to use various condiments (salt, fresh squeezed lemon) with each dish.

I've had tempura many times but none of it was prepared with the light delicate touch that Tempura Matsui chefs provide. Chose a Hokkaido-produced junmai sake called "Taisetsu" that was aged inside an ice dome for clean and refreshing taste. First course was Jackfish sashimi and Japanese pickles, followed by chawan mushi (egg custard) with seafood that warmed my tummy on a cold evening. 

Among my favorite tempura selections were uni (sublime!), whiting, okra, plump Hokkaido scallops and snow crab. There were three flavor selections for the last donburi rice bowl; I chose ten-don and it was delicious. Grapefruit jelly with whiskey cream sauce was a refreshing end to the feast.

Tempura Matsui is an intimate spot so it pays to book early, especially for coveted weekends. Very special experience overall.

no idea that such thing as a tempura omakase could exist, but here it is. i was very surprised by the omakase offerings (so i won't spill all the items that you got), but i was extremeeeeellyyy impressed by the chwanmushi and of course the tempura items. the service was very sweet and kind and they told us how to best enjoy all the items. in fact dining here inspired me to make my own tempura at home (of course not nearly as good).
If you like tempura then you must come here!

I visited Tempura Matsui for lunch and I made this reservation three months in advance. They offer only one choice of lunch menu with add on at additional cost. 

Service & Environment [4/5] - Friendly and warm services. Our servers taught us how to best enjoy the tempura and checked on us multiple times to make sure things are alright. This place is overall quiet but not to a point where you need to whisper. 

Food [3/5] - Lunch menu consists of a selection of tempura, cold udon, Japanese steamed egg, a small tray of cold dish and apple pudding. Two ways to eat the tempura: seaweed salt or special dipping sauce with radish. I prefer the salt as it enhanced the flavor the most. You can also order a bowl of rice at no additional cost. Portion was generous and we had the following tempura: shrimp, okra, shiitake mushroom, pumpkin, string beans, red snipper, onion and eel. My personal favorite was the string beans and pumpkin. No doubt they use fresh ingredients and the coating is crispy but flavor is lacking. Most of the items were bland.

For $55, the lunch special is truly amazing and very filling. All of the tempura was perfectly fried, and I really enjoyed the accompaniments. I do wish there was a little bit more of the initial dishes - or maybe for them to serve it after our first tempura course - because I didn't realize I needed to pace myself, since eating tempura straight for multiple courses in a row gets pretty oily. Not that the tempura is oily - it's set to rest on paper towels, and it's perfectly light and crunchy, but you know that feel when you eat too many fried foods at once :x The udon and cold veggies were great complements but I definitely finished them too fast.

The highlights for me were the maitake, shiso wrapped fish, shrimp, and kabocha. Everything was delicious, though, and I liked the simple and light dessert at the end. Overall I would definitely come back for an indulgent lunch. For some of my co-eaters, this was a bit too fast and they could not keep up, so do keep that in mind - it's a fast-paced meal, since the tempura is best fresh.

Wow this place was  great! I was expecting it to be a heavy meal, with everything pretty much being fried and all, but it was surprisingly not the case at all.

I did the higher end tasting menu, and everything was on point. The most unique dish I got was probably the tempura uni. I'ver never had uni fried before, and it was a very different way of eating it.

In total, I ate 23 things + 2 tempura items I added on! It was a lot of different things, and I think it was definitely worth it.

My most favorite item was probably the scallop tempura, which was not part of the omakase menu. It was VERY good and I would recommend you get it a la carte if you are also a scallop person.

Overall, I had a great time here. Everything was amazing from the service to the food. Check this place out!

Hands down the best food-related experience. This was my first time trying a Michelin star restaurant so it will always be a special memory. Initially, I requested counter seats so we could watch the chef work his magic but they informed me the day before the dinner that it was not possible. Luckily, we were sat at a table where I could still catch glimpses of the chef working. My family and I were so impressed by everything from service to the food to the ambiance, even the bathroom felt zen. 
I got the Tokusen Omakase Course ($220) which consists of an appetizer, chawanmushi, tempura omakase, shokuji, and dessert. We also got the lobster tempura ($65?) to share, a whole lobster divided and served with assorted tempura vegetables. The tail was served as tempura in small pieces so we could each take a piece and then there was a small dish consisting of plain lobster meat. Each piece of tempura served had a super thin coating of delicately crisp batter that complemented the main ingredient. We were also taught the best way to eat every item right when it was served. 
I was a little skeptical at first because the portions looked small, but as the meal progressed, the team had timed the food to come out in such a way that I was full by the end. Truly an unforgettable meal.

WOW did not even know tempura omakase even exist!! 

I was genuinely amazed at the experience -- usually you would like tempura all taste the same (because of the batter) but literally with this place, you taste the inside more than anything. 

I highly recommend for anyone whose looking for a new twist on omakases to look into this place! 

The tempura lobster course was one of the most phenomenal dish I've ever tasted -- also very very filling because of the rice at the bottom. 

Must try if you are in the city and down for an experience!

Fantastic spot for a special occasion! The lunch is affordable at roughly $60 with the option to add on uni. The presentation is impressive as they make the tempura piping hot right in front of you. The udon salad was refreshing and tangy, which is a nice contrast to the tempura (some of which can be a little salty but still light). I would recommend this place for lunch! 

Food: 5/5!
Ambiance and presentation: 5/5
Experience: 6/5

WOW 
Another solid tempura spot in NYC. 
I am so blessed to finally visit Tempura Matsui. Place is legit and they offer both lunch and dinner. 
Personally, I normally would be having food coma after eating fried food so I chose to have their lunch set.
Lunch set is light:
it is consisted of green beans, pumpkin, mushroom, onion, okra and trout.

Food is on point, delicious and their service is also great.

Come enjoy a great japanese tempura which deserves every penny

We came to Tempura Matsui for our anniversary dinner. We made a reservation for two on a Wednesday night. I would make a reservation in advance. Dining at Tempura Matsui is an intimate affair and they will book a week out. 

We ordered the Tokusen Omakase and Omakase. We also ordered two sakes as a suggestion from our waiters who were very knowledgeable about their selection on hand. We had great service throughout the entire course. The waiters explained each dish and instructed us in how to season the tempura dishes before taking our first bite. Tempura Matsui is Omakase with multiple rounds of small dishes, which were all very beautiful aesthetically. Both my bf and I were very ecstatic to try everything! My Bf particularly enjoyed the chawanmushi that came in the Tokusen set. For the shokuji (rice + miso), I particularly liked the truffle salt I got mine flavored with, which  also included extra truffle salt. The omakase set has a variety of seafood and vegetable dishes that filled me up quite early on but was enough for my bf. 

Overall very luxurious experience at Tempura Matsui. Would recommend for a celebration dinner in NYC.

Didn't expect it but, Tempura Matsui was outstanding. The location is great, just a little hard to find. So many good choices here, I was blown away with the menu, tried their Sashimi and it was excellent. Great. Excellent service and staff. It's perfect.

Fantastic food and fantastic service. My husband and I stopped by this weekend for lunch. The chef prepared a special menu for the sakura season. While I don't believe salted sakura was an ingredient in the dishes, every dish was prepared with thought and perfect execution.  The tempura was fantastic, perfectly battered and fried without tasting or feeling oily. The side dishes were impeccable and delicious. I also fell in love with the tempura ice cream and pear jelly. This restaurant has definitely earned its Michelin star.

I've wanted to try this place and finally did. Unfortunately it did not wow me.
Overall good tempura omakase experience. But I expected more. Maybe indoor dining in front of chef's counter would have been better.

Awesome lunch experience. The tempura was delicious, not very oily with a great texture! My favourite is the mushroom and scallops. 
The lunch set comes with a standard side dish with 3 different combinations of tempura sets - shrimp, scallop and eel with assorted vegetables.

The experience was unique and for that, my interest has been sustained.  Tempura dishes were ones that I had some, but not total exposure, when I visited Japan 2 years ago, primarily at Tenfusa at Tsukiji fish market.  It does speak to a naïve palate that needs a frame of reference, akin to a strapper who can't recognize cheesesteak greatness as it's being eaten, but the tempura at Matusi was light and crisp with a variety that I liked and found unexpected.  

We chose to ate outside, but when I did walk inside, I felt like I was back in Japan.  At this moment where international travel is *mostly* suspended, I was grateful for a moment to experience the nostalgia.  There is indoor dining--of this writing, a few seats at what I assume is the original omakase table, with 3 or 4 booths nearby.  Everyone is masked, gloved, and some goggled.

We had gotten the "standard" Omakase course, in lieu of the Tokusen Omakase course (~$60 dollar difference).  Nearly everything was wonderful, with the Japanese pumpkin, shrimp, scallop and Japanese eggplant being my personal favorite.  I felt full, and not disgusting, which feels like a huge win considering the type of meal being consumed.

Service was great, especially as they instructed how to incorporate the Tentsuyu sauce, salt, lemon, radish, wasabi, etc with each specific item.   

What I ultimately don't know is if tempura omakase is really a niche (at least compared to sushi), but for anyone wanting to have a unique experience, this is worth a try.
Spectacular meal for lunchtime, and a great price to boot. Personal highlights were the Japanese pumpkin and scallops, as well as the tea. Staff could not be kinder.

Matsui is, for now, seating outside. I suggest you run there while the weather holds out for the finest Japanese tempura in NYC. The price for the outdoor multi-course dinner is particularly reasonable and the service is always top notch, even by Japanese standards.
Fantastic tempura and great service in a very formal and almost monastic atmosphere. It's pretty wonderful but so quiet and reserved it's not going to be for everyone.
Tempura here is an art and the whole dining experience was a mindful meditation in quality ingredients.  Missing them during covid times!

Tempura as good as Kyoto - expensive, but transported back to Japan. Tiny restaurant, I think about 28 seats max (someone will correct me). I sat at the bar, where the action is, with 2 chefs working in coordination to cook Tempura, which is served as individual pieces, as soon as its cooked, with etherial light batter with almost no oil. Tempura was the highlight; Sakizuke and Sashimi were good, but not that special. Decent sake list. Nice 'suggestions' as to how each piece should be eaten, with salt, or tempura sauce, or lemon juice as appropriate.

Decided to try this place out as it has one Michelin star and my bf loves fried anything. It was a pleasant dinner, staff are extremely nice and attentive. We opted for the kaiseki meal and added the lobster. There were a few unimpressive pieces like the lotus root and some of the vegetable pieces but I will rate it 5 starts anyway because the lobster and scallops were phenomenal. We actually ordered another serving of the scallops - they were that good. I would go back just to have those again.

Tempura Heaven!!!

This place is so wonderful. From the moment that you step in you know you are in the authentic tempura place. Excellent service, classic decoration and chefs were all focusing on preparing your tempura piece by piece, right in front of you.

Their lunch special is definitely a great way to sample their food.  You will be having small dishes, soups to optional chawanmushi then onto the fried courses and wrap up with a dessert.  Whole lunch experience shall take about 1.5 hours. Reservation is a must.

Big fan of Tempura Matsui. Have to point out the excellent service this restaurant provides, from the initial check-in of the coats, to the attentiveness of the wait staff, to the constant refilling of drinks, and the explanations of each dish and how to best consume them. The quality of the ingredients were top notch, leading to top notch tempura. The side dishes were also impressive.

This was one of the best dining experiences I've ever had! I got the $120 set for dinner and it turned out to be a perfect amount of food. The tempura is perfectly cooked and not oily. The accompanying seaweed salt, lemon juice, and tempura sauce with radish complemented each piece well. My favorite tempura piece was the eel, followed by the shrimp head. The service was also superb--my water was always filled and an explanation of whether to use the salt/lemon juice/sauce was an excellent touch. Looking forward to eating here again in the future!

P.s. The host at the front was very friendly and made me feel very welcome! He was very personable and made an extra effort during the entire experience to make our meal enjoyable.

Also, check out the bathroom! They have automatic toilets that are heated and that raise the seat for you when you close the door--small details that make this Michelin Star restaurant earn its reputation.

Came here on a Saturday night and this place was packed! First time trying Tempura full course and it was a blast! Both food and service are amazing. Their uni tempura is my favorite. I had to take a pic even through I had taken a bite. Thanks to my boyfriend let them know it was our birthday and they came with a special dessert which was a lovely surprise.

I came to Tempura Masui with my husband for my birthday dinner. I was always curious about tempura omakase so was excited to come.

Atmosphere: 5 out of 5. Small, cozy, sweet feeling. Really felt like I was in Japan somewhere. Noise level was good and loved the whole feel. There was Beetle's music playing in the background which my husband loved but thought maybe a little mismatch but I felt happy and good.

Service: 4 out of 5. All the smiles from the staff and they were very helpful in explaining different tempura and menu. Only reason why I gave 4 stars for this was because after omakase when I ordered one extra piece of scallop, it took almost 20-30 minutes to come out which made the whole experience 2 hrs long in total. They did give me birthday dessert at the end which was cute.

Food: 4 out of 5. The tempura were fresh, clean, simple and delicious but it wasn't mind blowing different. Probably more authentic to simple Japanese cruisine. Thought the tempura will be more fluffy crunchy. My husband and I am small stomached so we ordered the smallest omakase and we were quiet full by the end of the meal.

Overall, great place for the special occasion and worth it for the service and atmosphere.

I came here for dinner and got the Tokusen. This is omokase-style tempura; absolutely amazing. It almost seems sacrilegious to review a place like this. Everything was pretty much perfect and even the meal pacing was great; a little faster than many high-end restaurants, particularly in this style although that may be in part because there were only two of us being served at the time. Definitely not too fast or rushed though. Reservations are likely required as there are only 6-8 seats at the counter. It looked like they had a few tables as well although I can't imagine coming here and not sitting at the counter. Warning: you won't be able to eat tempura anywhere else, ever again.

Was notified right on the spot that they don't have lobster tempura and foie Gras chawanmushi, which are the dishes I have been eyeing for. I have to say it is very unprofessional without notifying customers in advance. Would not come if I was informed about the fact first.

Stumbled upon this Michelin starred restaurant and my mind was blown.  I had no idea tempura could be so delicate and softly crunchy.  It is certainly an experience to be had!  Sitting at the counter, you are given the privilege of watching the chefs at work.   When they dip the batter, they do this elaborate dip and swing to get rid of extra batter and it is simply beautiful.  Any tempura is amazing, sushi is ok, but then again, why would you come to a tempura place for sushi?
I'm not sure if this place is worth the greater than 150 bucks per person. Overall food was good and service was great but pricey for what it is.

My husband and I went to this restaurant for my husband's birthday. But I was the one so excited because I love tempura. It was extremely great! Even we ate the fried food almost entire course We weren't feel so heavy at all. They served complementary desserts for birthday. That was super nice!! Service was excellent, they explain for each dish how we can eat to make the taste the best. It was kinda pricey but definitely worth for the money.

Have tried the restaurant twice and both times it was great. Would recommend the tasting menu and adding more pieces if you are still hungry. The fried prawn heads are crunchy and tasty. The palate cleanser was different each time we went but they all did a good job of resetting our taste bus between the course. Highly recommend the Foie Gras Chawanmushi if you can get it. Was a highlight of the meal along with the tempura. The tempura is the star and the chef is great at making sure the tempura is cooked perfectly without woo much batter or oil on the pieces. All the fish and the vegetables were fresh and great. The tendon is a great last main course and I like to get uni as a topping for it. Dessert changes but the grapefruit wine gelee was very good. Worth a visit if you want to try high end tempura.

I had high expectations and they were met (which is usually rare).  First off, the restaurant is a little difficult to find so look for a building named, The Nash since it's attached to it on the right.  

I had the Matsui Special Lunch Set which was an amazing value.  I had sake with my meal because...I like to drink and why not?  I don't know why I'm explaining myself.  Anyway, the decor was minimalistic with I believe, Japanese paper covering the walls (in the bathroom too).  The ceiling had bamboo architecturally lined with clean patterns.  I especially loved the ceramics.  The plates, bowls and tea cups were so pretty, unique and just fun to admire.  

As much as I enjoyed the decor, I thoroughly enjoyed the food also.  The chawanmushi was silky smooth with bites of seafood in it.  The bowl and lid for that were super adorable, btw. I dipped all of the tempura pieces into the salt they provided me.  I also dipped it in the tempura sauce with the grated daikon but the salt was so delicious.  It was kombu salt and it was a great complement to many of the pieces. My favorites were the Maitake mushroom, Japanese Red Snapper, crab and shiso, sea eel, and Japanese pumpkin (ordered separately at the end).  I ordered the uni and shiso at the end also but although it was good, it actually wasn't my favorite.  Nonetheless, I had an amazing meal and I was happily full.  I did not feel like I consumed too much oil or anything either.  Everything tasted clean and light.

So now I can't eat tempura anywhere else.  It was so light and crispy.  There's something special about chefs preparing the pieces of food one by one, in front of you and then eating it right then and there, whether it's sushi or tempura.  

I have to mention that the service was amazing, too.  I should've gotten his name but the gentleman was so kind and explained things so well. He had a fun sense of humor also, which is always a plus for me.  

I highly, highly recommend this place.  I can't wait to go back!
The best tempura in NYC. Who cannot like this place. The great atmosphere including the architecture. It is just gorgeous.

I found tempura matsui on Instagram,because it spreads abroad in Chinese community ,also it has very good reviews on yelp.we couldn't wait to give it a try,and made a instant reservation for last Saturday dinner ,anyway it turned out that servers were very welcoming attentive and friendly.chef took tempura job very seriously,kept focusing their attention on every tempura pieces ,food came out in very beautiful presentation with amazing good flavors. You will feel so enjoyable for a meal in such a nice ambience ,compared with Other Tempura makers in NYC ,I definitely will recommend this great place to  anybody who likes Japanese traditional food ,but specialized. 
For me ,experience you had in here absolutely deserved the price .

I have had tempura throughout Japan and the rest of the world.  The tempura at Matsui is just ok--nothing special and certainly not worth the price.  The place was very old style and dated.  I would not recommend this to anyone, especially someone that knows good tempura.

Great place. Definitely over priced but if you're trying to do a special night or impress someone, then this is the place. Staff is friendly and nice but they definitely take their tempura seriously. Special meal for sure-- wouldn't recommend for everyone though if you don't like traditional Japanese food

I had the $120 course like others and it come out with small appetizer then 2 pieces of shrimp tempura , 2 pieces of fresh water eels , 2 peppers,1 cauliflower, onion and eggplants .. not sure for all vegetables that from my course or from my friend's a la carte. Then a small bowl of shrimp tempura over rice with red miso soup and dessert . The service is very nice and polite but food is just ok . Not that delicious and everything come in a small pieces. It's a little bit disappointed for coming to have a delicious tempura in town. If it's delicious , I might not complain for how small and over price it is but it is not .

Where to start...

The tempura is, at a minimum, very good. Much is excellent. A few items, such as the whitefish + spine, are superb-- the baby corn was unexpectedly in this category. Some are too rich for their own good (uni tempura). And the scallop is truly amazing.

The three set menus, only the most expensive one includes the "chefs special set," and the latter is what we tried, which is a bit of a limitation.
