Other items-- ten don, the appetizer, etc. are very good but not sure they're worth the money. Honestly, the scallop was so good, the whitefish + spine, maybe the chilled tomato refresher and the grapefruit dessert were worth it; the rest, while good, you could skip.

Service is very good, watching the chefs' intense concentration from the counter is a significantly different experience than at other high-end Japanese places (for say sushi or yakitori), it's a solid experience if you can justify the cost.

Made reservations almost 3 weeks in advance for this place. My boyfriend and I knew this was one of the top places we wanted to go while our stay in New York. The restaurant was pretty hidden on the right of this hotel so it's easily missed. 

We each got the $120 set meal and one whole lobster to share +$68. The meal started with arugula, calamari and shiitake mushrooms in ponzu sauce. Super refreshing and a great way to start the meal. Then came the tempura shrimp heads, two tempura shrimp, okra, Japanese onion, Thai (red snapper), eggplant, and cauliflower. Everything was fried perfectly that way you don't feel greasy or gross afterwards. The whole lobster is a must! Definitely worth every penny. 

The service there was super attentive, wiping any spills you have on the mat and always refilling water after every sip. They were very informative of the food and explained to us which way was best to try their food (with tempura sauce, with seasoning, or with lime)
It's pretty pricy but worth coming back in the future
Best tempura in nyc- closest to what you will get in Japan. Consistently a fantastic experience to dine here.

The place was not big, very good place for a quite meal where you can truly focus on the tempura culture. The lunch set is very good, also pretty cheap, for 40$ you get udon, sashimi, appetizer, and tempuras, plus a green tea to end and a dessert.

Romantic date or great for four. Server staff is extremely professional and friendly. Food on in the spot for every piece of oma kase. Right when you finish, the next one is ready for you. Make sure you get the miso soup! The tempura is lightly battered and doesn't leave you with the heavy oil feeling. Each fried piece is truly as art masterpiece.

I know tempera and this hidden gem is better than tenors places in Japan. Testy and fresh tempura, made by a chef came from a famous Nadaman restaurant originally. Service is also nice too. Only down side is pricy (therefore four stars) so I can't go every week and I will be frequent for lunch ($40 lunch course), evening could be minimum $150. But whenever I have extra money I will come this place.

Made reservation few weeks ahead for counter seat just to get a better dining experience and see all the actions.
Me and my friend chose the more pricey Chef's special selection Teishoku (Lunch) because it's our first time here so why not go for the best choice available.

This lunch set includes: Shrimp, Seasonal seafood, Vegetable tempura, Rice, Sashimi, Udon salad, Miso soup, Seafood chawanmushi and Seasonal dessert. Sounds like a dream lunch right?

All the tempura were all freshly fried piece by piece. 2 pieces of shrimp tempura arrived first without crispy legs, sadly. I guess it's only included during dinner. The rest of tempura were Snow crab in Shiso leaf, Pumpkin, Sea bass, Maitake, Squids and Kakiage.

The main problem I had with most of the tempura here was the flavor. There was no seasoning whatsoever. I understand authentic Japanese tempura supposed to be very light and grease-free but what I had today was all of above with no flavor. Even the tempura sauce with grated daikon radish couldn't rescue those perfectly fried tempura.
And because they using all fresh, imported ingredients then the natural flavors should be stunning but that wasn't the case.
Also squids were unexpectedly chewy even though it was perfectly fried. 

The only positive highlights of the tempura were:
Shrimps - fine amount of natural sweet flavor from the shrimps.
Maitake - possibly the best mushroom for tempura. Maitake is delicious on it's own already but with tempura batter, even better.
Snow crab w/ Shiso leaf - great combination and flavorful.

Some of the side dishes were just okay. Decent miso soup and sashimi. Udon salad doesn't have much flavor, nothing to write home. Soba noodles would've been a better choice for tempura meal. 
But that seafood chawanmushi was a magnificent little side! As well as Seasonal orange jelly dessert.

I was a bit disappointed overall, especially for spending good amount of money for fine-dining level lunch. I honestly had better authentic tempura from casual spots like Hannosuke and Tempura Hirao Honten.

My husband has been wanting to come here for the longest time, and he finally surprised me for lunch one weekend and made a reservation for a date :) Unfortunately, I'm not sure we were blown away by anything we had that day. 

Since we've never been, we chose to go with the more expensive lunch specials. For $65, you get the chef's special selection teishoku which includes shrimp, seasonal seafood and vegetable tempura (the main reason why we're here haha), bowl of rice, udon salad, miso soup, sashimi, seafood chawanmushi, and dessert.

I'm not sure what kind of fish the sashimi was, but there were maybe 3 pieces of it and it didn't have much flavor. I was fine with that though since it wasn't the star of the show! The chawanmushi was outstanding, loved how silky the egg was and how much seafood flavor they got in there. The rice was cooked to the perfect consistency (I'm pretty sure it was good, but I'm pretty sure it tasted extra great to me because I had been going carb-free for a while haha!). The udon was also nice and QQ.

Now onto the tempura. There are only maybe around 10 counter seats that get first row seats to the tempura being freshly fried. One of my biggest issues was that there was no seasoning on any of these pieces, so they all kind of tasted one note. And I guess what we got served that day didn't really have much natural flavors in them :( I know you're supposed to dip it in the sauce with the daikon but it all started to taste the same. Here are the pieces we got:

Shiitake Mushroom - Not bad, but a teeny sprinkling of salt would have been perfect.

Shrimp - seemed slightly overcooked but it was good. I ate the shells too, totally edible :)

Crab in Shiso leaf - this is a personal preference, but I don't love crab. I gave this one to my husband to eat haha

Lotus Root - I thought this was pretty good, but nothing special.

Eel - Not bad, but I think I really expected something way more tender and more flavorful.

Okra - probably my favorite piece of the day, I needed something that would cut through the heaviness of tasting something deep fried for the entire meal. This was refreshing.

Squid - meh. Hated this, texture was so rubbery.

After you finish your meal, you get to order additional pieces if you're still hungry. We wanted to try the eggplant and the japanese pumpkin, which both turned out to be kind of subpar. The eggplant skin was so tough we had to pick them out, and the pumpkin texture just wasn't as fluffy as we expected...and it's not cheap! I think they were $8 for two small pieces. If you want any of the seafood, I believe it's around $25 for the two pieces.

The dessert I actually really enjoyed, it was a really creamy panna cotta tasting yogurt dessert with a tart jam.

Not sure how different the dinner is considering the price jump, but not sure I'd want to pay that for the tempura I tasted during lunch. I would much prefer Secchu Yokota!
best tempura! very elegant deco. Super tasty. Freshly made Tempura. Tempura sauce is also superb with strong refreshing taste.

Outstanding concept and environment, but I was not impressed with the execution. 

I ordered the seafood tempura lunch which comes with the tempura, sashimi, chawanmushi, and a dessert. I also ordered the uni to supplement the meal. 

I was not impressed with the tempura. While the batter was delicious, I found several elements to be lacking proper execution. The Japanese sweet potato was very dense and toothy. The scallop was good, but not anywhere near the level of the creaminess of protein I'd sampled in Japan or elsewhere in NYC. 

The chawanmushi, a Japanese egg custard, was flavorless and had on offputting texture somewhere between yogurt and flan. I'm not seeing the appeal of this dish. And I have eaten and enjoyed food extensively in Japan to know this is not a regional disparity in palates. 

I found the tempura dipping sauce with natto? to be very weak in flavor. 

The rice was well executed. 

The sashimi (some sort of white fish) was good, but of a grade, I'd expect in any decent sushi joint (still a bit toothy on the bite). 

The service was top-notch and the ambiance was incredibly close to being in Tokyo. 

Overall, however, I was not impressed with the level of cuisine for spending almost $100 for lunch.

So worth the price!!! The meal was incredible, the service was impeccable, and the desert was so light and delicious! The tempura was so fresh. I would give this restaurant six stars if that was possible. THANKS, TEMPURA MATSUI!!!!!!!!!!!

Loved it. You have to order the uni tempura. Snow crab was amazing and shrimp tempura was really good. If I have enough stomach space I would've ordered lobster and abalone and other things. You get full very quickly with tempura and the rice/udon/sides. Save it for next time.

I had a great lunch here, opt for the larger omakase. The tempura was so delicious. The portion was also just right. Service is pretty great, never had my water empty. The servers could try to smile a little more but other than that it was fun to see the chef cook tempura. He was very kind, and the orders were delivered in a very timely manner. 

Thank you Tempura Matsui, best tempura since my trip to Tokyo last summer.

This is a great restaurant with authentic Japanese tempura. Place is very small and cozy, seating a total of about 16-20 people. There are about 10 seats in front of the chefs, who are cooking all of the tempura in front of you. There are an additional 3 small tables behind this row of seats. You should definitely make a reservation here. 

There are 2 options for tempura: 1) all tempura served separately with bowl of rice on side ("Teishoku") or you can have all of the tempura pieces served together all at once with sauce mixed in over a bed of rice ("tenju"). I personally loved the tenju because having the rice seasoned with sauce was so delicious! However, I definitely want to go back to try the teishoku, which allows for you to taste everything fresh out of the fryer while it's perfectly crisp because they're cooking it on the spot and serving you 2 pieces of tempura at a time. 

Other than the tempura, the prix fixe menu comes with a bunch of other sides (udon, salad, delicious miso soup, scallop custard dish). The miso soup is definitely the best I've ever had. 

This is a very upscale restaurant, though you don't necessarily have to dress formal or anything. It's one of those places where they pretty much clean/freshen up the bathroom after each customer use to make sure it's always clean for each customer. They pull out your chair for you when you seat and fold your napkin when you get up, etc etc. FYI the waiters do hover a little bit but it's just the way it is. They'll be sure to tell you if you're eating something the wrong way. Despite all of this, the entrance is very underwhelming and looks like some random back door! (See photo). You really have to squint to see the restaurant sign. 

Highly recommend!

my husband and I came here for an early birthday lunch in mid-Jan. I was able to get reservations and had asked for bar seating in advance. This place is very unassuming from the outside, and we had almost missed it! However, it was lovely inside, with great hosts and an intimate atmosphere.
Upon walking in, we were greeted by the host, who took our coats and scarves. We were then accompanied to the bar (which was like 20 ft away haha) and given warm towels for our hands. He ordered the special lunch combo, while I had the regular one. The only mishap was that they had mixed up who had ordered what, and the things that they come with are slightly different. However, we were sharing so it wasn't a big deal. 
I was most excited for the scallop, but that, along with the okra, ended up being my least favorite. The scallop had gotten too cooked, and I don't really like okra in general.
The other pieces that we had were delicious -- my personal favorites were the shrimp heads and the snow crab wrapped in shiso. They were truly so light and crispy, and just sitting there watching the chefs made it a really great experience. 
To top it off, dessert is included, and we received this creamy custard like dish with orange jelly like stuff on top. SO GOOD. It was the perfect, light end to a heavier (but not heavy considering everything is fried) meal. I'd come back just for that.

This place is #1 on our must go list for our NY trips. The location is unassuming and the service is friendly and welcoming. When we asked the host to take a group picture for us, he insisted that we all go outside in the freezing cold (which he was not dressed for) and took multiple pictures for us. Starting off the experience with such a nice host was so great.

We made reservations for 5 for Friday lunch and he recommended the bar rather than trying to squeeze into a booth. After coming here, I would say that even if I had the option, I would go for the bar. The guys in our group got the Special (larger) menu while the women went for the regular. Do not get the Tenju, especially if you're sitting at the bar. You'll get all of the tempura cooked at once on a bed of rice. With Teishoku, you get the pieces one by one so you get to enjoy it as soon as it's done.

I can't imagine coming here for dinner because even the lunch was SO filling. There's also a big gap in price.

We're going to Tokyo next month so will be looking for places like this there, but can't wait to come back to NY to visit this great restaurant!

This place was amazing. Truly eye-opening to see the artistry involved in making tempura. Definitely pricey but still a delicious and unique experience. You get to watch true experts at work. Try and get a seat with a good view at the bar. Lunch omakase is a comparatively good value. Everything was delightful including the absurdly fancy  toilet in the bathroom.

Eating here is bittersweet. The food is so impeccable, you can't help feeling a tinge of sadness that tempura will never ever be the same again. Firstly- go for lunch. The lunch omakase here has got to be one of the best deals in the city. I went for the larger omakase ($60) and was extremely satisfied. I was presented with a beautiful tray with a chowanmushi, sashimi, bowl of rice, pickled vegetables, miso soup and salad - all beautifully assembled.

Now the tempura. Those accustomed to the thicker eggy batter will be in for a surprise. The batter is light and delicate and the oil in which the goodies and fried is the clearest cleanest oil I've ever seen (the chef and his sous chef are constantly straining it of impurities). The light delicate batter allows you to take the freshness and the flavors of the underlying vegetables/seafood. My favs included the shrimp pancake (chunks of plump shrimp molded together), the king crab, the shitake and of course the uni. The uni is a supplement but SO worth it. Uni tempura sounds like blasphemy but not when done so impeccably. 

All of the sides were excellent too- everything was done so simply but so well- allowing the flavors of everything to shine. The hamachi sashimi was so incredibly fresh and was complemented very nicely by some simple greens. The service was of course excellent- but even if it wasn't, would definitely come again and again for the food.

A tempura themed restaurant. The dishes are so beautifully presented and not only the tempura, everything else is tasty and fresh. The service is really good too. I recommend lunch deals so valuable. My husband got the 40+ set and I got the 60+ set and we shared each other's dish. We think that's the right way to do it. The portion of the dishes are very generous

The ambiance was very cozy; service was professional. The restaurant  me back to one of Tokyo's fine dining restaurants. I had pre fixed menu (the second choice); I was too full by the end of the meal. The tempura was light in taste, not oily and heavy like most tempura that we know of. Definitely will come back for a la carte menu.

Made a last minute lunch reservation here over the phone; the gentleman who answered was very accommodating. The food was solid but I was more impressed by the overall experience. The quiet and soothing ambiance, all the little perfectly arranged plates, the presentation of the sake in beautiful crystal glasses, the helpful server, etc. made a simple lunch so enjoyable. We got the $60 lunch special: from best to worst, we enjoyed the scallops, mushroom, shrimp (2 ways), fish, lotus root, squid. I made sure to get seats at the bar so we could watch the chefs, but the room is pretty small so I would say this was unnecessary and will opt for a table next time. Pricy, but would love to return for a special occasion!

I think everyone should try this place. The restaurant is small and cozy. They're ordered in sets. I got a lunch special for $60. The order comes with a lot and I didn't finish all of my order. The food was great though . The service was amazing, the waiter was very patient and answered all of my questions. Totally recommend this place if you're in New York.

Tempura Omakase!
***
Locals 
Perfect for people who love Tempura! Especially omakase!
***
Travelers 
This place is world renowned and one of the few Tempura omakase locations! If you've been to Japan, this is the closest to Tempura from Japan in NYC.
***
My Recommendation 
Come for the lunch special! Definitely a lot cheaper than dinner, but you get options on lunch sets. You get noodles, appetizer, and dessert. Come by if you can! Definitely make a reservation in advance and try to sit by the counter to see it in action! The restaurant is tucked away at the side of a luxury condominium, so ask around if you're confused.

IG: @foodisseur

A very unique and delicious experience!

We were able to get week of reservations for a party of 4. We were told we would have to squeeze as they didn't have space for 4 but worked out perfectly and we were all comfortable. Very small, intimate space. Only place a party of 4 or more could fit spaciously at a space is the tempura bar. 6 adults (family and plus ones) were cozy and happy at a table!
Food was excellent and super interesting. We got the Chef recommended tasting menu ($220/pp) and two lobsters. Each lobster is supposed to be for 2 people but between the tasting menu and lobster, splitting between 3 we all left very full. We also split the pickle appetizer, which has a variety of different items that were pickled.
Service was great, very attentive staff.
Bathrooms were also very memorable. Totos are a Japanese type of toilet, which they had installed. The memorable part is that the toilet seats were heated! 
Recommend when you're looking for a different experience for dinner. Certainly haven't had anything like it in NY.

A wonderful place to go for a special occasion. Exquisite food and service. The course menu will make you leave the place so full and satisfied. I also love how the interior transports you to Japan! Extremely cozy but still spacious. I highly recommend this place :)

Tempura like no other!  This place was simply amazing from start to finish.  The service was just as excellent as the food.  The tranquil setting was the perfect ambiance to enjoy a meal of this quality.  I don't always take stock in the Zagat / Michelin star ratings of restaurants when it comes to Asian cuisine but I must say, I can "taste" why this place earned their Michelin star.  I had the pleasure of dining here with a friend for my birthday and boy was this a treat!  

We had prime seating, where I could see all of the action (only 9 seats available at the intimate chef's counter so note that you want to sit there if you make a reservation), which is highly suggested.  We watched the chef prepare each delectable item - he pulled out ingredients from a specific selection of the day, from a special wooden box.  I got to watch the whole cooking process -- first lightly tossing the ingredients into the bowl of tempura batter and then gracefully slipping it into the hot oil for cooking.  Alongside the chef, his sous chef worked quickly - in charge of the cutting board and of plating every morsel.  They are a good team - very much in sync.  I dined on the seasonal omakase menu and my friend had his own "custom" vegetable tasting selected by the chef.  (Note to the vegetarians, the batter contains dashi, which is a Japanese soup stock made from fish, eggs and kelp).  This is disclosed on the menu but I'm mentioning it as well just in case.  

Each piece of tempura was refined, succulent and as flavorful as it looks. 
 The concept, so simple and delicate.  Each item encased by this light golden batter; still retaining it's natural flavors and textures.  As each "floaty" piece of tempura was presented to us, the chef would tell us which spice or condiment it should be paired with for maximum enjoyment.  As in my photo, the spices and condiments are all placed in front of you, so use however much you want to enhance your experience.    They even had a silver pinching apparatus to squeeze the fresh lemon so you didn't have to get your hands dirty. Genius.

The premium seasonal omakase is a delight.  I have never had the luxury of eating tempura abalone, squid, tilefish, scallops, and King crab (just to name a few).  It's premium alright!  Each tasting more delectable than the previous.  Also part of the seafood omakase, I had toro sashimi with sea urchin, foie gras infused chawanmushi (this egg custard also contained mushrooms and  chicken), chef's choice of seasonal vegetables, and a final course of tendon.  SUPERB.  I can't recommend this dining experience enough!

Side note:  for my vegetable loving friend, he had a custom menu of three kinds of mushrooms (oyster, nameko, and enoki I believe), Japanese eggplant, okra, string bean, and pumpkin to name a few.  Every piece was amazing.  

From start to finish - some amuse bouche in between tastings...every taste was elevated.  What a privilege it was to dine here.  This place is good for groups (larger groups are seated in the dining area and not at the chef's table).  Excellent for foodies alike, as each tasting course steps it up to the next level. The portions are small (individually) but the tasting menu is far from skimpy and very satisfying overall.  You'll be stuffed!  

There is an a la carte option too if you don't want to do the Omakase. Totally a special occasion should you be willing to splurge ($$$$) - totally worth it.

WOW , probably the cheapest Michelin restaurant I ever been too and it is worth every single dollar!!!

Service was excellent as expected, I was able to sit in front of the chef so it was neat to be able to see how he prepared everything.

Food was GREAT, you get to choose the house made soba noodles paired with rice and a variety of the tempura the chef fries you up. 

Never knew tempura could taste this good, changed my perception for life....must go

Truly exemplary tempura omakase experience. The service, the chef's choices- all superb. As good as in Kyoto where I first had tempura. The king crab, shrimp, and mushroom will blow your mind. It's pricey but totally worth it for a special occasion.

Nice place for a visit. I'd love to sitting at the bar table watching the chief making tempura.
The service is excellent.

We met for a business lunch last week and had a magical experience. The tempura is light and lovely. An tempura experience like none I have had before this day. The sauce was exquisite, served with fresh grounded radish that you add to the dipping sauce. It was simply divine! 

The service was impeccable. My napkin never hit the floor and if it did I had a replacement in a moment. If a sprinkle of soy sauce spilled onto the table by accident, it was wiped fresh before you could say oops. Not only were they attentive, but genuinely friendly. The meal was memorable and their efforts and attention to detail were greatly appreciated.
Nice hidden tempura restaurant with a good collection of sake. Staff are super friendly & helpful (in recommending the drinks!). Don't miss the lunch set: they are quite a deal!
Top precision and care with every detail of having a fine dining experience, from tempura preparation to attention with service. Great experience! Thank you, Tempura Matsui!

Wonderful. Just like in Tokyo. Had a wonderful meal. Very reasonably priced. Stupid full at the end. A just lovely experience all around. Small restaurant, so get a reservation ahead of time, but for a Saturday lunch we got one last minute. 

If you enjoy tempura, as a meal, this is a must visit.

This place is a scam. Please stay away. 

They advertise fake prices on their website. When I inquired about the prices I saw on the website they wanted to negotiate with me. This much for this much and so on. When I said but I saw this price. They said they would do it, in a whisper. 

Also, not a single person eating here was Japanese. This is not a good sign. I have been to japan over 10 times and let me tell you, this is not the real deal. 

STAY AWAY.

Came for the prix fixe lunch and ordered the $60 menu. 

We sat at the bar so we were able to see the chefs make each individual order. My favorites were the jumbo scallop tempura, the fish + shiso tempura, and the kabocha squash. Surprised that the shrimp tempura wasn't one of my favs considering I normally love the shrimp. As for the rest of the prix fixe set, I saw rave reviews for the cold seafood egg custard (chawanmushi) but definitely didn't feel the same way. The seasonal dessert was a mango pudding that was alright, but again, not blown away. 

Overall, I wasn't wow'ed by the food though, given expectations that I had for a michelin-starred tempura place, but it was still an enjoyable experience. Might be more worth it to come for dinner, which I would definitely consider.

In a city full of sushi omakase, my sister and I wanted to try something different. We ended up making reservations for lunch here on a weekday. The entrance is slightly hidden to the right of an apartment on a street I didn't even know existed (Tunnel Exit Street). Upon making our way, we were seated at the counter where all the magic happens.

We opted for the regular Tempura Teishoku (40) and the Chef's Special Selection Teishoku (60). With teishoku, they cook it one at a time and place it on a plate for you omakase-style. With tenju, I believe they prepare everything like a bento box (with the tempura all on the bed of rice).

Watching the chefs prepare at piece and wiggling them around in the deer fryer felt like some work of art. The oil in the deep fryer was crystal clear. Each piece of tempura was battered very thin, crisp, and just right. I couldn't taste the oil, but rather could really taste what was on the inside. And often times, we think of tempura as just shrimp and vegetable tempura. Of course, that was not the case. We had snow crab, scallop, fish, shrimp heads, and other things that swim under the sea. And each bite was unlike anything I've experienced with seafood before. The tempura coating really opened up the palette of each piece and transformed it to something else.

Consensus: best tempura I've had in my life. I'm sure I can find better somewhere deep in Japan, but being in New York, this Michelin star restaurant is the closest to tempura nirvana on this hemisphere.

Reservations required.

Great tempura from a welcoming chef and staff. The tempura has always been on point here and the star of the show. Staff is always friendly and warm.  Restaurant is nicely decorated. At dinner you have three fixed menu choices. Have gone for the midrange ~$150 and left content and happy but not overwhelmed.  Would recommend to anyone for a nice night out. 

Sit at the counter!

Food: 4.5/5
Interior 4.5/5
Price (lunch menu 40-60 pretax pretip)

Visited for lunch during a weekday for the lunch menu. Ordered one of the $40 menu and one $60 menu. The basic layout of the lunch was similar, with some differences in the vegetables and seafood. 
My favorites of the lunch were scallop tempura, fish tempura, mushroom tempura. The soy sauce base was not too overpowering, which was perfect as a dipping sauce. Also, it was nice to see the chefs actually prepare the food freshly in front of me as i sat at the counter. At first, the speed of the food was a bit too fast, and I asked for a slower preparation, and the chefs accommodated immediately. 
Sizeable portion of rice, soup, and some pickles are provided. I asked for extra pickles because I wanted something more refreshing, contrasted to the tempura. 
Great value for the amount of food and fresh ingredients, Would love to come back for dinner in the future.
The tempura is pretty good and the lunch set is very cheap for a Michelin star restaurant!

I can only say nice things about our experience at Tempura Matsui today. I called to reconfirm and asked if we could sit at the counter. Host was obliging and could make the adjustment. We were given a warm welcome. Wonderful decor. Would have thought you were in Japan. . We chose the $60.00 lunch. Waiter helped us choose Teishoku sake. Went perfectly with all the food. We initially received a tray with sashimi, miso soup, salad, pickled veggies, shrimp in a custard, and sauce to dip tempura in. 
We watched as the two chefs cooked each piece of tempura. Prawns, sea bass, king crab, scallops and shrimp, fish cake, okra, Japanese onion, and hen of the wood mushrooms. Onions were  not notable. Everything was perfectly cooked. Almost more than we could eat. The meal ended with a lovely mango pudding. A bargain!!  
Will definitely return. Like being in Japan.

My first michelin restaurant in New York! After trying the "upscale" tempura shop in a mall in Fukuoka, Japan, I looked for another similar experience in the states. 

I never knew Tempura could be considered "fine dining" and served like sushi. Tempura Matsui is a much smaller restaurant than the one I ate at in japan, and the chefs are much more careful throughout the process. 

From beginning to end, the service was amazing! Althought I had to -1 star because in terms of taste, the mall shop in japan still won. Maybe it's an unfair comparison to something from the motherland, but I felt like the tempura's here were pretty much the same after the first bite. 

The first bite was glorious, and then the rest of the textures were pretty much the same whereas the one in japan featured a lot more variety. 

Finally as for price, Tempura matsui started at $150/pp for their lowest end menu whereas the shop in japan was $30 for a standard meal. 

Either way, if you don't have the opportunity to visit Japan, Tempura Matsui is a great alternative to experience high-end Tempura.
Like the thin tempura coating and fresh ingredients. Great texture of seafood and good side dishes. However, consider kinda pricy for lunch set.

Here me and my partner ordered $165 course set.. & sushi platter.. their tempuras taste so good. And every course menu is so new and filling enough :) (we had to step outside to take a break in between the tempuras and the main course) But the course menu overall price i think is a little bit higher than it should be.. i r

Great ambiente and friendly service. The decor is simple and elegant. And the staff is welcoming. The menu is mostly prefix but the a la carte selection is towards the back of the menu. Atmosphere is very personal and exclusive, consonant with the price. Enjoy!!

Only good things to say. Great food, great service, good space. 

It's like a sushi restaurant, but with tempura. Sit at a counter (or at a seat) and they cook the tempura right there in front of you. It's so good. Yes, it's fried. But it's not too oily and it's fried perfectly light and crispy. And even though you're eating a whole meal of tempura, you don't feel heavy or bogged down by oil or fat. It's great. 
It's very difficult to find tempura so nice like this.

So i'll break this review up into three parts as always: the service, food and then drinks.

Service: Both the host and waiter were attentive and accommodating to anything my party had asked. My cousin and I made sure that we must be seated at the bar. When going to a omakase style restaurant you have to seat at the bar to be able to talk to the chef and experience how dedicate they are to their art.

Food: The tempura itself was light and not oily like how most place service their tempura. I have to say that I appreciate that because with their menu, you're going through 8 courses that in itself is a lot of food.

Drink: I recommend the Yuzu Omoi with the dish. With fried food i usually like to drink something refreshing so that I don't feel bad about how much i just ate. This sake has a nice lemon/orange citrus flavor that cleanse your palette.

Amazing tempura that is light and airy. Truly exceptional experience that opened my eyes and palate of what tempura can taste like. Had the lunch Chef Selection Teishoku at the counter. Tempura was placed in front of you piece by piece right out of the hot oil. The pan of oil was clear like water throughout service w the chef diligently scooping out the batter bits, which were given to you for udon/soba course. I also loved the end of the meal soup thickener to be poured in the soba sauce.  Would love to try the bar menu next time in NYC.

We came on Friday and asked a la carte menu. We ordered two set of Karuma Shrimp, Japanese Whiting(Sakana) , Kakiage, Sea Eeel, King Crab, shiitake and Hokkaido Sea Urchin. 
Eric, our server, provided all different type of "dipping sauce", such as tentsuyu saunce or ten-don with radish (the most common one), salt, salt with green tea powder and a steel press for lemon juice. Eric is super friendly and passionately to explain what vegetables/seafood they made and what sauce to accompany and bring the best of taste.  
Every tempura is prepared fresh and delicately fried piece by piece.  Each item is veiled of light bright-yellow color and sealed original freshness, flavor and texture.  
" If you still think fired veggie and shrimp equals to tempura, you are totally wrong."
Every ingredient contains some waiter, more or less, so how to coat the ingredient as thin as possible to achieve gold-light coating tempura but still enhance its original flavor? In what temperature to fry the food and for how long? The frying time varies as every ingredient is difference and it requires years of training and experience that kind of skill sets a pro apart! No wonder that Tempura Matsui has been listed a Michelin starred restaurant two years in a row. 
Matsui set a new standard on my tempura experience

We got the medium dinner course, and it was honestly too much food for both of us. But it was beautiful, meticulous, delicious, and inventive throughout. The staff was very accommodating and kind as well, especially since we had to take the courses slowly due to a health issue. My favorite was the mushroom tempura and the tomato/apple/mango palette cleanser. The only miss for me was the grapefruit jelly but that owes more to grapefruit than than the kitchen. I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious even simple fish bones could be, which is saying something because I'm not usually keen on them
Amazing Japanese food !! Just love it!! Been here few times and always have tasting menu..the customer service always wonderful.. my favorite lobster tempura :) will be back soon !!

This was a special and amazing dining experience.  The chef cooks each tempura fresh, right in front of you with so much care and passion.  Each item we ate on the omakase menu was crispy and delicious.  Even though the food is fried, strangely it was NOT greasy or heavy at all.   We would definitely dine here again and highly recommend it to others.  Worth the money.

Such a wonderful restaurant.
Can't believe I waited more than a year to revisit TM.
A treat to watch Executive chef Chikano meticulously prepare each tempura.
Not only are the tempuras standouts here, but all the appetizers that come before are, as well. But, I was sad not to see the scallop/nori tempura no longer on the omakase that I ordered. Why??? That was one of the best restaurant dishes, imo. I love tencha, and they prepare one of the best ones here. Add uni and their tempura, and you got the perfect dish.
First time having a whiting bone tempura; It had the texture of a chip and was so delicious.

Must order the 'whole lobster' tempura upgrade, which comes w/ maitake & pepper tempura. At $58, that's a great value. Still thinking of that dish.

Hope to visit again soon and try the lunch menu.

Excellent service.

Highest recommendations

: 10 calendars

Def one of the finest tempura in town! It was a very pleasant experience watching the Chef and his assistant/apprentice making tempura from the raw fish and flour mix. People were really nice - they would explain to you what vegetables/seafood they made and what kind of salt/sauce compliments the best.
I got the basic omakase and my friend got the premium. Ordered chawanmushi with foie gras and extra piece of lotus root on the side. Great prawns(heads was definitely the highlight). Pumpkin and shimeji were very tasty too.
Their tempura keeps the original flavors of the materials, maybe it's their style(I think). Heard there are other places that might give you more surprises like you can't even tell what it is anymore. If you expect something like that of that they separately cook veggies and seafood you might still have to go to LA.
Overall it's a great experience and good value. Might bring my other foodies friends there again especially for huge Japanese food fans.

Definitely worth every penny!!! 

The tempura is super light and enhanced all freshness of the seafood. I had the Tempura Teishoku and it was delicious. The tempura sauce was SOOOO good, served with fresh grounded raddish added into the sauce which brought out the sweetness of the dipping sauce. My son had the Tempura Tensu and he devoured everything. 

The service is impressive; staff were attentive and explained every course served. We never had to request for anything!

Advanced reservation via Open Table to dine during lunch. Reception was friendly and warm. Set menu for $40+tax and additional charges if you decide to have extra tempura. Pick the bar seating so you can enjoy the chef frying and prepping your food. One of the tempura (squid) that was served to me was still raw on the inside. The Shrimps were tiny so that was a disappointment for me. 
The shitake mushroom was nice and juicy. This was an extra order for $8/pc. overall its a nice experience but not the best.

Are you kidding me ??? We had dinner here and expected  sophisticated Japanese cuisine. The atmosphere and service were excellent but the food was very plain,  without anything memorable.  The tempura was great but did not justify the high price. Waste of money.

I have been here a few times and i have always been satisfied. Overall, It has one of the best tempura pieces i have had. The batter was light and airy, crunchy and yet dissolve quickly once you bite it; therefore it doesnt make you feel heavy after. The flavors are always fresh and rich and the temperature is always on point because they make it there in front of you and serve it right away! The other courses that go along with the tempura tasting are good but the most exciting part is definitely the tempura pieces. The service is good and i also like the ambience. Warm and cozy!! Definitely give it a try! :)

A nice and quite Japanese restaurant. Great environment and the waiter and waitress are super nice and helpful. Food is also good. It's my first time to a tempura special place. However at the end of the day, it's still fried stuff and pretty heavy.

Very important thing about the menu:

The difference in the 3 price levels are not only the difference in how many courses but also the quality of tempura. As in, the higher priced set gets tempuras like abolone, kisu(japanese whiting) which the other ones don't and must order as an extra. 
____________________________________________________________
I ordered the $165 set and i very much enjoyed the anago and the snow crab. The scallop was disappointing because it was almost entirely cooked as opposed to the one i had at secchu yokota which was almost raw and very soft and sweet.

Services was nice but a little awkward at times with the waiter seeming newish and the chefs being soft spoken (they try and tell u the name of each tempura and the recommended sauce but they have to say the same thing to everyone which is hard task for them).

It was a good to try but don't imagine coming back often.

I love, love, LOVED my experience at Tempura Matsui!  Everything from beginning to end was wonderful.

There was one very minor occurrence in the reservation stage -- I made a reservation for 7 p.m., but the night before I received an email from Open Table which said my reservation was for 6:30.  I called the day of and a gentleman answered the phone and called me by name before I even identified myself (thanks to his recognition of my Hawaii area code), so I was already impressed!  He also said it was fine if I preferred to come at 7 but that they would be ready for us at 6:30.

The food and service were impeccable.  I also appreciated that this is a very small, quaint restaurant.  Most of the other restaurants I visited on this trip were busier and sometimes a bit hectic, so it felt good to be in a more relaxing environment.  Each of the staff were pleasant and did a great job of explaining everything.  The quality and presentation of the food were also amazing.  My friend and I got the lobster add on -- if you like lobster, do it!  It is so worth it!  Upon a conversation with the server, we decided on the Kaiseki menu and added the lobster, and it was a good choice.  We left feeling very satisfied.

I would highly recommend Tempura Matsui and want to return again!

Saw a video of this place on Facebook and instantly wanted to come. My favorite Tempura joint is in Tokyo. Since then, Tempura never tasted the same ever again. I went to one in LA and it did not compare. 

The service here is 5 star and so is the food. Every serving was just so tasty. The batter was very light and fluffy. The uni is bomb! (But so is every dish!)

Pricey but so worth it!
So amazing! Can't believe the chef has spent 26 years working with this! The waiters are all kind. I will definitely go there a second times

In short, Tempura Matsui was a joy I've seldom come across in my life. Unfortunately, I don't think my vocabulary is enough to fully capture the awe-inspiring experience I had here and do the restaurant the justice it fully deserves.

I was here to celebrate a friend's birthday, and we managed to get reservations at right in front of the chef - if you're able to, I highly recommend this, as watching the show made the experience that much better. There are three courses to choose from: Tokusen ($220), Kaiseki ($165), and Irodori ($120), from which I opted for the mid-tiered Kaiseki course, along with the lobster supplement, which will run you an additional $58.

Very rarely do you get to witness something that turns everything you assumed you knew about food on its head, but Tempura Matsui is a restaurant that has managed to unlock that secret. Tempura usually leaves me feeling bloated and disgusting, primarily due to the exorbitant amount of oil and grease, but to my surprise - and inexplicably great pleasure - nothing I ate that night left me dissatisfied.

Each ingredient was extremely high-quality, from the mushrooms to the lobster (which I would highly recommend, even with its supplemental price), and treated with so much respect that it was impossible not to savor every bite slowly. Before the chef proceeded to the next selection, he would pause a moment to make sure the tempura was made to your liking, and with your nod of approval, would then continue creating art.

Overall, while the price was nothing to scoff at, my only regret was not following my gut and going with the Tokusen course. The silver lining there is that this gives me a reason to return to experience it all again.

I've had some great tempura before in both Japan, Hawaii and LA, but this takes the cake.  The deluxe menu is $220 and comes with a lot of food.  The tempura is not oily and the variety is mostly expensive items.  Not much vege fillers which I like.  

The toro and foie gras starters were absolutely delish.  The the tempura just came and came and came.  From shrimp to king crab to abalone to uni, to lobster, everything was excellent.

It all ends with either soba, tendon or tempura on rice in tea.  A little grapefruit ice to end the meal.  You will absolutely be full at this point.

Service deserves Michelin stars as everything is explained,  plates changed out often, drinks refilled when needed.  

Tempura Matsui please come to Hawaii!

After a particularly stressful session of clinic, my friend and I decided to forego our usual $6 Halal cart next to school and instead decided to opt for lunch at the Michelin star rated restaurant. 0-100. As if we're already dentists. 

I had this place bookmarked for a while and knew of the $40 prix fixe lunch option. It might not be fair to rate this restaurant without getting tempura omakase-style from the bar, since undoubtedly getting all the tempura pieces at once as part of the lunch set takes away from the quality of the experience. 

The entrance is next to a hotel, easy to miss, among the boring office buildings and residential complexes of Murray Hill. Once past the curtain you are ushered into a Zen-like wooden interior that offers a brief reprieve from the city. 

The lunch set came with an assortment of seafood and vegetable tempura served with or over rice, a small appetizer and your choice of soba or udon. Now for $40 I know I shouldn't have been expecting much but I was a wee disappointed with the paltry two pieces of ebi shrimp and anago (saltwater eel). The tempura coating was light and clean with a minimal oily taste. The delicate exterior gave way with a satisfying crispy to yield the juicy interior. My favorite from the veggies were the maitake mushrooms and shiso leaf. 

My only gripe is that everything comes out at the same time for the lunch special. The tempura can't help but get cold and soggy after sitting for a while. The green tea pudding for dessert was delectable tho, and served as a nice cool-down from the rest of the meal. I would definitely advise sitting at the bar for the full experience.

I had the best memory in this restaurant with my favorite person. From the warm reservation called, friendly stuff, Amazing chef. They really hooked me up. The food is amazing. They took tempura to the next level. You will never think tempura can be so clean as stream. Everything are just on point. 
Side story- the price is not kidding expensive. But I want to say it's worthy. I will give 4 stars because of the price. Just sat I had the best date in my life, I give 5 stars

If you're serious about tempura, you should probably check out Tempura Matsui, a restaurant that treats tempura like high-end sushi. I went for lunch with my mom while we were visiting New York, and we had a tempura meal unlike any other I'd had before.

Tempura Matsui is an enormously expensive place where you can get a $220 per person kaiseki dinner, but if you're curious and feeling just a little indulgent, lunch is far more reasonable. The $40 prix fixe comes with a seasonal appetizer, tempura, noodles, and dessert. You can add onto that with extra toppings or a la carte tempura, but it won't be because you require the calories.

The restaurant was beautiful, with a small, intimate dining room built around a tempura bar, where a couple of stoic chefs prepared tempura one piece at a time. We sat watching them at the counter, soothed by a Beatles soundtrack and the soft continuous sound of frying. Service was great. Our waiter was warm and professional. I'd developed a blister while walking to the restaurant, and he brought me a Band-Aid, which I applied in the bathroom--a very nice bathroom, by the way, with a state of the art Japanese toilet.

The food was spectacular. The lunch set came with a choice of tempura teishoku or tenju, and a choice of homemade soba or udon. We got one of each option and shared everything, and this was the way to go. The sets came on these gorgeous trays laden with rice and tempura and noodles and all the dipping sauces and condiments and a la carte toppings. The appetizer came on there too, taking up one little corner of the lunch set. This was a luscious little block of corn tofu, dense and creamy and sweet, topped with tofu skin, jellied string bean, and goji berry.

The tempura options sounded almost identical on paper--"assortment of shrimp, seasonal seafood, and vegetable tempura served with a bowl of rice and pickles or on a bed of rice and pickles"--but they ended up feeling pretty different. For the full Matsui experience, I'd recommend the teishoku, the one with rice on the side. The tenju is a rice bowl, so all the tempura comes at once, arranged over rice with a drizzle of a sweet soy-based sauce. With the teishoku, you get the tempura fresh out of the frier, one or two pieces at a time. It's kind of like sitting at the bar at a sushi restaurant instead of at a table. Same food, but the presentation is more fun at the bar.

As you might have gathered by now, the tempura was ridiculously good. The batter was thin and crispy, shattering nicely with every bite. The tempura pretty much kept all that good texture even in the rice bowl, where it was dampened with a touch of sauce and close proximity to warm rice. I actually loved that sauce--it made the rice addictive, and enhanced the tempura, providing a more assertive flavor than the lovely but mild dipping sauce. Both the teishoku and the tenju came with shrimp, squid, eel, shishito pepper, mushroom, sweet potato, onion, shiso, and carrot tempura; two pieces each, except for the eel, which was enormous, fried with leaves of shiso. Every single piece was fantastic. Really hard to pick a favorite. We had the option of ordering more tempura a la carte before dessert, and we ordered one piece each of the uni, the snow crab, and the kisu, or Japanese whiting. (The chef obligingly split each piece in two.) I'd never had uni tempura before, and liked it less than I thought I might, but was happy to try it. It came fried with nori, and the heat did some interesting things to the texture. The snow crab and kisu were two of the best items of our meal, just phenomenally good tempura.

The noodles were also superb, homemade soba and udon served cold with dipping sauce, scallion, and grated ginger. We sprung for a few of the a la carte toppings: plum shiso, salmon roe, and sea urchin. Both the soba and udon were fresh and springy, delicious with the dipping sauce and luxurious toppings.

For dessert, we had little cups of roasted green tea pudding, dotted with three red beans. This was nice, creamy and delicate and not too sweet. A great way to end our wonderful lunch at Tempura Matsui.

Japanese Whiting is FANTASTIC!! Fried to perfection! 
Salt is very salty. So be cautious about the amount.
Snow crab is also pretty good. Shrimp is amazing but not as impressive as I imagine.
I won't recommend squid though. 

Great service and experience overall!
epic. i did the lunch set. it was so good i cried. top level tempura like they do in japan

Absolutely loved our lunch here.We sat at the bar and watched the masters at work. Each item was tempura'ed individually, with much care. The lunch set ($40) is significantly more affordable than the dinner menu so be sure to make it during their lunch hours! 

The door is quite easy to miss. Look to the right of the entrance to the hotel and find the green fabric that marks the entry to the restaurant.

I came here for lunch and have never had such bland and expensive Asian food in my entire time in NYC. Also, it's in the middle of nowhere and you have to walk through curtains to enter a pretentious dome. There is literally only one meal on the menu you can order and the portions are tiny. Granted the display is aesthetically pleasing but the food itself tastes like nothing. The rice tastes like it came from a bag heated in a microwave for too long and the seafood was likely the scum of the sea. What a waste of $40.

Had Good Friday off so I couldn't give up the opportunity to try the lunch special at Tempura Matsui. This place is easy to miss as it is attached to a nice apartment building but once found, this restaurant itself exudes simple eloquence. We sat at the tempura bar, enabling us to watch the chef make fresh tempura for its customers. 

For $40, this meal was well worth a try. There was plenty of food to leave me feeling happy full. We got an assortment of shrimp and vegetable tempura on top of rice with a side of hot udon and little vegetable small bites. Everything was really delicious. There is a difference in broth between the soba and udon which was impressive. The udon had more of lime taste while the soba had more of a lemon taste. The tempura itself was just a tad softer than I would like it to be but the ingredients were splendid. Shrimp, peppers, squid, mushrooms, etc.
At the end of the meal, we got some tempura vanilla ice cream. Also very delicious with a good hit from the fresh strawberry on the side. 

Overall, a great meal!

Had the lunch special which is an amazing prix fixe for $40 and allowed me to try Tempura Matsui without the $$$ price tag associated with dinner.

There was only bar seating plus 3 or 4 tables when I arrived but there seems to be additional rooms in the back. 

The tempura was made in front of my eyes! Such a neat experience. Food was super good and service was impeccable. Would return!

Came in for lunch and had the only item: lunch set with appetizer, assorted tempura over rice, soba, and dessert. Great intimate atmosphere, attentive staff, amazing tempura; expensive but justified. The tempura is really on a heavenly level, light delicious and not one bit oily. Awesome experience overall and highly recommended.

My experience here was absolutely phenomenal!
I paid extra for the lobster supplement and it was definitely worth every penny.

It's a very small restaurant with only 3 tables and seating at the bar (technically it's not a bar, but I guess the chef's kitchen?). Due to this, setting is very intimate and the waiters are very attentive.

With the 5 course menu, I assumed I wouldn't be that full, but boy I was so wrong. I felt like I had to be wheeled out by the time I was done. Each time our master chef would lay down a piece of tempura, he would give us instructions on what flavors to layer it with, making our meal not only delicious, but interactive. Each piece of tempura was lightly fried and the flavors were so delicate and crispy. 

The only downside to this place is the location, it's not easy to get to; but on the plus side, you need a good walk to the subway after that large meal.

I came here to try lunch with couple girl friends today, I was impressed by the service, but no so much to the food. The host and the waiters were so sweet and so attentive, the service itself was no doubt a 5 stars. The food, however, made me disappointed. The lunch set is $40, but I really can't see the value of it. It was a tasty and lovely meal but it was just too pricey from my point of view. I also paid extra $15 sea urchin as topping on my soba but i did not like the taste of it. I wonder if the dinner will be better than lunch, but given the price ticket for the dinner is so steep (dinner is going to cost $200 ppl), I doubt I will ever return to try the dinner.

Michelin 1 star restaurant, second year maintaining its rating. Evening is Kaiseki dining and lunch time is prix fixe menu of noodles, tempura, and dessert. Japanese fast food essentially but very good quality. For $40 it's a steal as the tempura tasted just like what I had in Tokyo. Egg custards are delicious. I ate all of them and then some. Noodles are house made and the broth was light and delicious with perfect texture. Kaiseki is not available in San Francisco, no such restaurant. Period. Though at Izakya Rintaro you can sort of get a taste of it. So dinner is a great place to start here but if you don't have time, lunch is a nice taster.

My favorite is their chawamushi or egg custard, very flavorful with plenty of seafood, The tempura is not as crispy as you'd expect but that's actually expected given it's served with rice and it's actually the same way I've eaten in Japan. In Japan it's also somewhat soft in texture but the inside is crunchy. Just not something you see here often in America. This may be the most authentic one just yet. 

Service is perfect and dessert is delightful.

All in all, the best meal to start a day is not breakfast, it's Japanese lunch. Let it be a Michelin Star Japanese lunch that does not serve sushi please.

I came here recently with my client for dinner and disappointing.. Don't get me wrong, all food except Tempra were not bad( so I gave 3 stars) but considering the price... Will never come back.. I don't think this restaurant will last for 300 dollar per person... No way... It's the part of Otoya so maybe they can survive but owner ( which is Otoya) should change the chef asap.

I had the lunch pre fixe. Service was very professional and attentive.  The tempura came over a box of rice so was a bit soggy but that may be the style. Regardless, it was delicious. The fish in shiso leaf was my favorite.  Udon noodles were also chewy and well done. Egg custard had generous amounts of seafood

The cheesecake dessert was fairly standard

Since it is a very famous tempura restaurant in NYC. I went there for lunch. The tempura is not that good and the price is very high. For $40, I got 2 small shrimps, 1 small fish and some veggie. You can see that from my pictures.  The undo is just a regular undo that you can buy from supermarket. I like the tempura in MITSUWA NJ is better and worth for every pennies. The service is very good and the restroom is really good and clean.

There are very few restaurants where they specialize in Tempura. A better way to say is that they do not exist in the USA.  Not only specialize, but the chef has to be the master in Tempura. Tempura is not Fried Vegetable and Fried Seafood. 

New York use to have Inagiku, but now that is gone, we have a new one in New York. This place is the best that you can get in the US. So if you like Tempura, you have to try this place. You will not be able to eat the Tempura at other restaurants anymore.

Looking for an empty, expensively-decorated and very Japanese establishment (whose staff is not all Japanese) ?  Looking for tiny portions, prepared meticulously in front of you should you have a counter seat ?  Looking for tempura king crab (first time I've ever tried that and it was fantastic), the likes of which probably cannot be found elsewhere in the Island of Manhattan ?  Then this is your place.  On a Monday night it was dead, and the meal was very expensive, and the location off the beaten path, but I'm glad I tried it.  Reminded me of Tokyo.

Although it has beautiful ambience and excellent service, it's pretty pricey.

Food was excellent but I wish my lunch TEMPURA was not on the rice with sauce because it lost the light crispness I was looking forward to and evaluate the tempura batter they made to do it.

The only authentic Tempura place in NY. It is a must visit every time I go to NY now. 
Was everything I expected and more. 
The location is easy and the overall experience of watching the chef make everything in front of you reminds me of Ten-Ichi in Tokyo. It is as authentic as it can be. 
The staff was excellent and kind. 
The 180 menu was plenty of food and included the King Crab. I'd have done without the Uni though. Everything else was amazing. 
Can't wait to go back.

So sad that chef Matsui passed away, what a master of his craft.  A true loss.

We came in via the Gilt City discount.  I was worried that it would be a reduced menu or they would leave off the "good stuff" but in fact it was a super filling kaiseki menu.  Everything was perfectly prepared with great attention to detail.

I have to say, the sake list is really over priced.  There are a couple of lower priced options on the list and ironically, they are the best suited for tempura anyway.  Go for those!

I dined here with a gilt city voucher for the kaiseki menu. The staff is amazing, so polite and kind. The space is casual and low key, very relaxed. Sitting at the bar gives a perfect view of the chefs. The experience was quite unique and special- I don't know of any other restaurants in NY that specialize in tempura. And the tempura here is unlike any other I've had. 

I started with a refreshing seasonal soup, followed by sashimi. You are given a few dipping salts and sauce, and the chef tells you which to use for each tempura. Don't be deterred by the fried shrimp head, which looks bizarre but is so crunchy and delicious. The progression of lightly fried tempura is fun to watch and fun to eat, and surprisingly not heavy. You have a choice of rice, soba, or noodles in tea broth (very refreshing) topped with some tempura seafood. My dessert was a matcha ice cream, which seems so typical but tasted so elegant. 

As the regular price is around $180-230, this is definitely an expensive dining experience. But there is so much attention to detail and the staff are so generous (the manager even gifted us a Michelin guide as he saw we were admiring their Michelin star plaque) - this is a unique Japanese experience that is worth a visit.

Although I am not big fan of tempura, but I am so impressed by this place. I totally enjoyed my food here, every detail was perfect. I may forget what I ate a month later, but I will never forget how amazing the service is here. It was far beyond my words. The service really made the dinning experience to another new high level. Actually, It might have been the best service I have ever experienced. ( I even can't believe I just said it, considering I have tried almost all  michelin three stars and two stars restaurants in nyc). 

I do agree it is really expensive , for myself, two dinks, some appetizer and extra tempura pieces, and tips, totally around $430. But considering overall experience, I think it is totally worth it. I will suggest it to my friends and love to come back again.

Decided to give this place another try after seeing the Gilt City deal of dinner for two for $200, a 50% discount off of the normal $200 per person price. 

This time around, the experience was very different. Start to finish, the service was warm, attentive... Really just perfect. We were introduced by name to the new chef, freshly arrived from Japan with 20 years of tempura under his belt. The maitre d' came by several times mid meal to check in on us. 

The food remains solid... Fresh ingredients with such a thin tempura cost the vibrant colors of the okra, shrimp, and crab come through as though they weren't coated at all. This time around, each items was followed by an introduction and recommendation of which salt, lemon, or tempura sauce to pair with each item. 

My one real hesitation about giving that fifth star is again the regular price. With the 50% off, the total still was nearing $$160ish a person when you add in drinks, tax, and tip, and that's with the discount. If I come across another Gilt City deal, I would most likely pull the trigger again, but I just can't see spending $200 a person before drinks, tax, and tip. 

Overall, the second time around was a much better experience, and a year later, the place is much more in their groove.

AMAZING food - beautiful presentation, perfect taste. This was my first tempura kaiseki experience, and a whole new world has opened to me. I was never a big fan of tempura before, but this "authentic" tempura experience I can definitely get behind! I devoured everything, even dishes and parts of ingredients I normally don't eat (e.g. shrimp heads, etc.). I just loved all the tempura items, especially the whole fried smelt fish, soft roe and the shrimp heads (truly special). Plenty of food to fill you up, but even though the shrimp tempura over rice was already pushing at our limits at the end, we still opted for a couple of add-on items (tempura scallop and uni) which were certainly highlights.

The service, as is the case with most upscale Japanese establishments, was impeccable. The restaurant itself is VERY low-key, tuck away in the ground floor corner of a residential highrise. In fact it took me 5 minutes of standing directly outside to find/notice it.

The only downside is it does seem to be a bit overpriced, especially the add-on a la carte options -- but you just have to try them because they'll likely be extra delicious.

Outstanding tempura course. Just returned from a 2 1/2 week visit to Tokyo last Monday where I dined at Tenichi Honten in Ginza, the flagship restaurant of one of Japan's most famous tempura restaurants. The cost is comparable, but I give Tempura Matsui a higher rating on both food and service. That's saying a lot because Tenichi serves great food and has impeccable service. My wife and I are half-Japanese, we're raised in Tokyo, visit Tokyo frequently and eat at the finest restaurants wherever we go. I read some 3 star reviews and it is clear that the reviewers know nothing about high-quality tempura or, in some cases, are ignorant about traditional, premium Japanese food in general. 

It was our 1st time at Tempura Matsui and I was not expecting it to be on par with the best tempura restaurants in Japan. I was so impressed, that I booked another reservation for 2 weeks from now. I will take one of my business partners who will be visiting from Southern California and a Japanese friend who I know will also appreciate the high quality.

Pricey, but as good as the best tempura places in Tokyo, where it would cost more. The tempura was wonderful, not the least bit greasy, and you could really taste the freshness of the ingredients. The other course were memorable too--the starter, which was an asparagus mousse, the somen palate cleanser, and the chawanmushi with foie gras and crab. I was too full for the rice course. I highly recommend it to any one who wants to eat tempura as it should be.

All in all, this was a very memorable meal, not only because of the cohesiveness between each course, but also because of the quality of ingredients as well as the mastery of skill. This dinner completely changed my perception of fried foods, as having grown up in Hong Kong, my understanding was that food items were fried to mask the "non-freshness". For example, it would be heresy to deep fry, rather than steam, a live and kicking, 2-catty heavy red grouper (東星斑). And yet, here I was, pleasantly surprised and impressed how deep frying accentuated the freshness of the ingredients. The price here is surely steep, $200 a pop, but for the eyeopening experience and immaculate service, I think it is more than fair. Really interested now to see how the menu would change based on the seasonal availability of ingredients - a cry to the omakase selections at a top-tiered sushi-yas.

Full dish-by-dish review can be found here:

http://www.higrubandgrog.com/stories/2015/11/12/best-fried-food-tempura-matsui

This place is amazing! It is a bit expensive (effectively $300ish per person including tax tip), but def worth trying at least once! 

The tempura courses were delicately and gracefully prepared with precision, and the entire experience was very memorable. Our waiter was superb, attentively explaining every singe dish - what each was made of and how to enjoy it. Chef Chikano was wonderful too. He's new to NYC and still working on his English, but he tried very hard to be polite and friendly to us and tried his best to communicate. I very much appreciate his efforts and his warmth. 

The palate cleaner dishes were great too! The cold soba noodle was very refreshing, and I LOVE THE CHAWAMUSHI - it was so rich and smooth! It's def one of the best Chawamushi I've had in my life (though the black truffle one at Brushtroke was pretty good too).

Dessert was probably the only lackluster dish - just green tea ice cream with cherry and coconut milk. 

Overall, we had a wonderful experience and I really recommend it!!

Went there because of the gilt city coupon that was essentially half off the 6-course meal for two people. Great experience. Service was very attentive. I liked that the chef always walked you through what garnishes to eat with the different tempura servings. The plateware is also quite beautiful. My favorite thing was surprisingly the sweet corn tempura. We also ordered tempura uni (which was interesting) and tempura shishito peppers in addition to the preset menu.

I had such a wonderful dinner at Tempura Matsui. From the friendly hostess to the food, everything was excellent. The tempura batter was so crispy and light, and was not oily at all. The sashimi appetizer was excellent. This place is worth a try if you truly appreciate Japanese cuisine and hospitality.

The most amazing service and food! I took my mom here for mother's day dinner on Saturday May 7th and was blown away by their extremely friendly service and outstanding food. I thought I was back in Asia. Every server was so friendly, polite and courteous. I thought it was even better service than Per Se or Le Bernardin, certainly beating any Japanese restaurants in the city including Yasuda, Ushiwakamaru, Azabu, Seki, Gari, etc. Their service is nothing compared to Tempura Matsui. Just go there and you will see what I mean.

Sad to hear that Chef Matsui passed away but we had chef Chikano right in front of us who just flew in from Japan last week. He was amazing and watching him make tempura was like watching an artist! I will never see tempura the same way ever again. Everything was so delicious. Tempura batter was so thin and perfectly crisp. Standout dishes of the night included fried scallops (barely cooked, it was like having fried ice cream, so fresh, so full of flavor) and fried uni (supplement to tasting $15).

First off, our server Eric was awesome and so sweet!  What a nice treat it was that our friends took us to...definitely doesn't even feel like we were eating fried food at all!  The price is definitely steep but it was quite an experience

The restaurant interior, chefs, waiters were all very Japanese style. A beautiful, cozy space focused mainly on the bar with the chefs frying, use of bamboo throughout, and soft, warm lighting.

The sakizuke was a scallop tartar with peas mousse and uni sauce. The scallop had a soft, delicate texture. The flavor of the dish mostly came from taste of the mousse and the uni sauce.

The otsukuri was an assortment of sashimi, starting with some seaweed and thinly sliced radish, very thinly sliced grouper, botany ebi pressed with kelp, and slices of blue fun tuna. 

The tempura course consisted of two shrimp heads, followed by one shrimp tempura, another shrimp, tender greenbean, squid, shiitake, king crab, spring ramp, onion, and sea eel tempura.

After the tempura, there was kuchigawari, a palate cleanser of firefly squid and cockles, and a slightly sweet, but savory miso sauce (reminded me of a light mustard.)
 
Then tendon, shrimp tempura over rice, with a pretty savory miso soup on the side and some oshinko. A cup of hojicha accompanied. This dish filled up any remaining empty space in the tummy.

A soybean dessert with simple garnish of sliced grape and mint leaf was presented in a beautiful blue cup with brown sugar syrup on the side. It was very enjoyable. 

The whole meal was finished with a cup of sencha.

This was an experience to be slowly savored over two hours. It was good but pricey for tempura.
I'm not much for words or anything fried but this place is just incredible . The service is as god as it gets . Worth every dollar.

This place seems really special, I just felt like they were close to achieving the greatness they're after but not quite hitting the mark. The menu didn't feel like a logical progression despite being delicious and providing some unusual combinations. The three stars is grading on a scale, their standards are high so mine are too. The service was impeccable and felt very intimate. It was an impressive display, just felt like a first draft instead of a final cut.

Also the bathrooms are incredible the toilet literally seemed excited when I walked in the bathroom.
Very clean spotless establishment, typical super friendly staff that treats customers with omotenashi. Tempura was perfect, everything was perfect. Pricey but great experience.

Was very disappointed.  
The tempura batter was light, and did not feel like is greasy at all - so that's a plus.
But everything else just really didn't live up to the expectations.
Go to Ten-Ichi in japan - much better quality ingredients for the price!
We paid extra for the uni and scallop - those turned out to be the best dishes.  But for the amount of money we spent, was expecting more.  Sashimi was just ok - not that memorable.  Presentation was decent, staff was attentive and service was great.  We had a server in training, so some items he couldn't really explain it well, but we can tell he was very nervous and still learning.
Don't think i'll be going back, there was nothing memorable.
The food is pricy for what it is. However, it's the attention from the waiter, chef, the experience and intimacy that adds the value to it. Everything was good and dessert also was amazing!

Truly a unique experience, the food probably deserves 4 stars too. The only reason I gave 3 starts is solely due to how expensive this meal was. I would still recommend going once, very authentic and the food was great. Service is very attentive and very traditional Japanese style. Loved that part of it!

This place is amazing and really under-publicized. Perhaps because tempura in general is not as well-known as its other siblings in Japanese cuisine? This place is truly wonderful. To advocate for the tempura-making technique alone deserves attention. The food here is delicious of course and of a wide array of choices.

Matsui is so Japanese style. They keep the original Japanese feeling from decoration, service to the taste of food, everything brings me back to Tokyo in one second. 

Don't worry the food is not enough for you. Even tho they seem like very little pieces, they can stuff you well. However, they balance all the food pretty well. Tempura are very light battered and not very oily, but if you eat like 10 pcs you still taste the greasy. Their tempura sauce is a perfect cure for grease. The Ten-don is so good I finished two bowls (my friend can't finish hers lol). Their dessert is divan!! 

Have to say this place is a bit pricy. Two people for 500 dollars + tip. Not a place that I can come back anytime everytime  when I want to eat their food but I'll come back some time (:

I was really looking forward to going here when they opened up this past summer and just went here for a birthday to partake in their kaiseki dinner.  First and foremost, they make the best tempura in the city.  The tempura is artfully made such that even though the fried morsels are served on a sheet of paper that paper essentially stays dry.  Though the tempura was the star of the show, the other courses were delicious with beautiful presentations.  The service was top notch with the waiter or the tempura chef describing the dishes and explaining the proper way to enjoy each piece of tempura (you get an assortment of condiments including tempura sauce, lemon juice, miso salt, or rock salt).  The sake selection was top grade as well.

However, given the price point, I'd only come back for an extremely special occasion.  Between the base meal, extra course of tempura, and one bottle of sake between four people was over $300+/person.  There are other omakase/kaiseki experiences throughout the city that I think may be of better value, but the tempura here is unique for New York and the level of service matches the price point.  It was definitely worth the experience. Make sure you get a seat at the bar to watch the chef at work.

I used to be so jealous of Japanese people as they had Michelin-starred restaurants for tempura, skewers or even sukiyaki. Now after Torishin won its star for skewers, the newly opened Tempura Matsui accomplished a second goal of nailing another star. Well done!

Matsui was very much humble judging from the outside, with only a small icon towards the right. It was also tiny inside. As there were only nine seats at the bar and three booths for small group sitting. Only Kaiseki was provided here - starting with assorted sushi/sashimi, followed by signature tempura, and ending with a shrimp tempura don. I actually enjoyed listening to the sizzling of tempura cooking as it reminded me my dad cooking at home back in China...every single dish was remarkable and among them, my favorite was the uni tempura - rich flavor with light taste.

Our waiter was so attentive that made us even feel like at home. Felt like Matsui definitely worth more than one Michelin star and I'm looking forward to enjoying another meal when it gets upgraded soon!

The price ($200+) for the kaiseki omakase here is out of touch with reality. Check out the photos to see what was in the tasting. I added the scallop ($15 per piece) and the uni ($15 per piece) to the tasting. My favorites were the shrimp and the uni. Everything except the tempura was a filler course and did not add anything positive to the experience. The tempura was definitely exceptional and not oily, but the ingredients used could have been of much better quality or more exotic appeal. The servce was great, with the server suggesting which salts or sauces to pair with the tempura.

Excellent service, dining environment as well as the food were surprisingly pleasant and authentic. Yes, it's a very expensive restaurant but the moment I stepped into I felt like I was in Japan again. Our waitress was very patient and explained everything as well as her recommended ways of eating different kind. The plating was super delicate and the portion was just about right for me. I would say the experience worth the expense. Hope they could have something new for the preset menu when I go next time.

Ok.  This is a place to have a unique experience (and unless you're rich its a one time experience).  The tempura truly is the best I've ever had.  Here's how you know this tempura isn't like any other.  The coating is very thin and at the end of the tempura part of the meal there are just a few spots of oil on the paper on which the tempura is placed.
